Primary Function of Position
The Advanced Procedure Sales Manager plays a critical role in driving identification and adoption of new or certain targeted procedures on the da Vinci surgical system.  Partnering with sales leadership and staff in Clinical Sales, Capital Sales and Key Accounts, the Manager will identify and develop Key Opinion Leaders to pioneer and expand use of the da Vinci system in surgical specialties in varying stages of growth.  They will also partner with local sales representatives to coach, counsel, and train them on selling to specialists in their assigned hospital accounts.  This role is part of a strategic team, senior level sales professionals across the country who are focused on identifying and expanding the adoption of procedures that will drive the future growth of Intuitive Surgical.  The APSM operates as an overlay to the Clinical Sales Representative (CSR), bringing specialized expertise, deep procedure knowledge, and hands-on execution capability to accelerate adoption of targeted procedures — specifically hernia repair, foregut surgery, and bariatric procedures.
Essential Job Duties
Driving measurable increase in targeted procedure volume (Ex. hernia, foregut, bariatrics) within assigned accounts, tracked against baseline and growth targets established in the account plan.
Procedure targeting could shift based on organizational focus.
Build sustainable surgeons in designated programs
Build clinical and economic reference centers.
Build new technology reference centers with strategic products like stapling and vessel sealer curved.
Sell platform value propositions to increase assets
Lead fellowship training initiatives.
Define short-term and long-term milestones for procedure adoption, from first case to routine utilization.
Regularly review and update growth plans to reflect account changes, competitive dynamics, and new opportunities
Aligning growth plan priorities with CSR and field leadership to ensure consistency with broader commercial strategy.
Leverage available data tools, market analytics, and data reporting to inform planning and track progress against targets
Work with clinical & capital team assisting and guiding MSA strategy and tactics.
Lead team clinical and technology competence
Achieves Quarterly and Annual Quota Aligned to Compensation Plans
Develop Key Opinion Leaders (KOL) in bariatric, foregut, and hernia surgery.
Assist in strategic surgeon targeting
Through collaboration with sales leadership, conduct strategic market development activities
For KOLs, execute all sales activities in support of developing their proficiency as a da Vinci surgeon.  These activities include: Select appropriate case observation site
Conduct on-site and wet lab training
Bringing value in first series of cases
Bring intra-operative & post-operative clinical value in initial surgeon case series
Development and leadership of advanced regional training programs
Serve as the market intelligence liaison for marketing and training teams
Conduct hospital and surgical practice executive and business alignment presentations
Elevate Area Specialty Sales Competency
Provide feedback to enhance representatives’ ability to sell in targeted procedures that are of current focus to the organization
Identify area needs, coordinate and run competency programs with support from VP and CSD
Manage Key Initiatives for clinical and technical excellence
Aligning with Sales leadership and marketing to manage surgeon training resources related to utilization, training effectiveness and procedural volume outcomes
Required Skills and Experience
Candidates would have demonstrated experience in leading through/by example and Cross-Functional Leadership
Deep knowledge of stapling and energy products
Proven Ability to Develop KOLs w QTI Data
Proven Ability to Use Data and Analytics/Business Acumen in Order to Develop GAP Analysis and Target Lists
Experience with Ecosystem Messaging and Capital 5-Pillar Process
Candidate for role would be someone with expertise and experience in: Developing KOLs in CR, GS, or TH
Demonstrated ability to manage complexity and work in an environment of change
Proven ability to influence peers
Effective communication skills across a broad organization with a variety of focuses
Excellent clinical selling skills and ability to quickly build credibility with a highly educated customer base
Track record of individual sales excellence
Management experience or management career track required
5+ years of medical device sales required
Bachelor’s degree required
Overnight travel required. Ability to travel up to 60%, dependent upon account distribution
Success in introducing new technologies to the market is a plus
Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience required

The Clinical Research Intern will join Intuitive's Future Forward Advanced Research team for a 10–12 week summer internship, reporting to a Senior Clinical Research Scientist within Future Forward. This role reports to the Sr. Director, People Tech & Digital Employee Experience. The Director leads and develops the product management and global Learning Management System (LMS) administration teams across the US, India, and Mexico, and builds a scalable support model as the function moves into People Technology. The role partners with IT and Quality Management to keep the platform reliable and compliant, and with Learning & Development, HR, Procurement, and Finance organizations to deliver modern, easy-to-use learning experiences.

Key Responsibilities
Global Operations & Service Delivery Oversight
Provide leadership oversight for global LMS operations and service delivery across the US, India, and Mexico, working through the Tier 1 and Tier 2 Operations Managers.
Use data, ticket trends, and user feedback to set SLA, quality, and satisfaction targets and to identify where service can be elevated.
Review performance with the Operations Managers on a regular cadence and hold them accountable for results.
Simplify operations by standardizing and automating processes, knowledge content, and reporting, and by removing duplicative work.
Set priorities and guide capacity and investment decisions to balance sustaining support against transformation work as demand grows.
Establish the controls and standards that keep LMS operations accurate, secure, private, and audit-ready, including how approved changes are implemented and how completion records and objective evidence are archived in the GxP system.
Serve as the executive escalation point for critical incidents and for cross-functional and vendor issues.

Lead the product management team and the global LMS administration team of managers, administrators, and contractors, aligning both to a single product vision and setting clear expectations, goals, and accountability for results.
Develop the team through coaching on complex technology decisions, defined career paths, skills development, and succession planning, building a leadership bench and cross-region capability.
Foster a customer-centric culture focused on learner experience, accountability, continuous improvement, and learning.
Manage workload and priorities across the team and the employee/contractor mix.
Promote agile ways of working and strong cross-functional partnerships across HR, Quality, Technology, and business teams.

Maintain service continuity, compliance, and audit readiness throughout the transition, with no degradation in SLAs or user experience.
Align operating model, governance, tooling, and ways of working with People Technology and Digital Employee Experience standards, and identify opportunities to share services and capabilities across People Technology platforms.
Lead change management and communication for the team, stakeholders, and users.

Translate business needs, voice-of-customer input, and enhancement requests into a prioritized, scalable roadmap with clear KPIs and measurable outcomes.

The SRPM will collaborate with cross-functional stakeholders to identify evidence needs and priorities and support the development and execution of evidence-generation strategies and research plans. This role oversees the initiation, progress, and conduct of evidence-generation studies, including those conducted by internal scientific teams, Intuitive-sponsored studies, and studies conducted in collaboration with external research partners. Collaborate with da Vinci and Multiport program leaders and cross-functional evidence stakeholders to identify evidence requirements and gaps, align on evidence priorities, and develop evidence strategies and plans.

Graduate degree in life sciences, medicine, medical sciences, engineering, computer science, data science, or a related field.

Proficiency in a second language.

Primary Function of Position
The Staff Mechanical Design Engineer independently owns technically demanding mechanical and electromechanical subsystems for robotic systems. You will lead subsystem architecture and detailed-design decisions, resolve complex multidisciplinary problems, and contribute to integration decisions beyond your assigned subsystem.
This is a hands-on individual contributor role combining mechanical design ownership with technical guidance and mentorship. The role reports to a Manager of Mechanical Design Engineering in New Product Development.
Essential Job Duties
Own subsystem development from concept through verification and design transfer, including mechanical requirements, specifications, design-risk analyses and verification documentation. Support validation activities with the responsible functions.
Lead subsystem architecture decisions. Compare alternatives and justify tradeoffs.
Design precision mechanisms, joints and actuation assemblies. Select and size components such as motors, bearings, transmissions, brakes and sensors based on operating loads, motion requirements and expected life.
Use first-principles calculations and simulation to establish load paths, component margins, structural stiffness, dynamic behavior and fatigue life. Check assumptions and correlate models with test results.
Create and release CAD models, manufacturing drawings and design documentation. Apply GD&T and tolerance analysis to functional interfaces, assembly requirements and inspection.
Build, test, debug and iterate prototypes. Develop test methods and fixtures, investigate failures, and verify corrective actions.
Work directly with suppliers, supplier engineering, sourcing and manufacturing to resolve technical issues, improve DFM/DFA and cost, and prepare designs for transfer.
Collaborate with systems, electrical, controls, clinical, human factors, manufacturing, supplier engineering/sourcing, quality and regulatory partners to resolve requirements and subsystem interfaces.
Lead technical reviews and guide other engineers’ design and analysis approaches. Plan technical work across functions, set priorities, resolve risks and mentor engineers through problem-solving.
Required Skills and Experience
Experience developing robotic or complex electromechanical products in a regulated industry, with demonstrated independent subsystem ownership from concept through design transfer.
Working knowledge of design controls, risk management, verification and validation.
Deep expertise in first-principles mechanics and precision mechanisms, with demonstrated ability to perform stiffness, dynamics and fatigue analysis.
Proficiency in GD&T, tolerancing, materials, DFM/DFA and manufacturing processes.
Experience designing rotary or linear joints, sizing components, and justifying decisions through analysis; integrating actuation and sensing; and collaborating effectively with controls and electrical engineers.
Hands-on prototyping experience, including assembly, testing, debugging, and rapid iterations.
Proficient with CAD, simulation, and PLM tools such as SolidWorks, ANSYS, and Windchill.
Demonstrated technical leadership through design reviews, cross-functional decision-making, stakeholder influence and engineer mentorship.
Experience with risk management activities including FMEA, risk mitigation, and reliability assessments.
Required Education and Training
Required: Typical minimum Bachelor’s degree plus 12 years of relevant experience, or a Master’s degree plus 8 years, or a PhD plus 5 years.
Preferred: Master’s or PhD degree in Mechanical Engineering or a related discipline.
Working Conditions
On-site four days per week in Sunnyvale, CA.
May involve extended periods of computer-based design and analysis work.
Must be comfortable occasionally working in lab environments, including prototype assembly, mechanical testing, and safe use of standard mechanical tools and fixtures.
Must be able to occasionally lift and handle 25 pounds.
Travel: 10%, including occasional visits to supplier and manufacturing sites.
Preferred Skills and Experience
The following skills and experience are not required but represent attributes of an ideal candidate.
Experience developing Class II or Class III medical devices, particularly surgical robotics or medical device capital equipment.
Direct application of standards and documentation frameworks such as ISO 13485, FDA QMSR (21 CFR Part 820), IEC 60601, ISO 14971, and DHF.
Experience supporting production launch, manufacturing scale-up or post-launch reliability investigations, and applying those lessons to new product designs.

Primary Function of Position
The DaVinci Specialist (DVS) will provide expert clinical & technical support, build, customize and coordinate education & training to physicians, nurses, and hospital staff on the use of DaVinci surgery, devices and therapies. This role partners closely with the sales team, specifically the Clinical Sales Representative and Clinical Sales Manager, to ensure safe and effective product adoption and quality control while driving positive patient outcomes.
The DaVinci Specialist is a dedicated program execution & clinical education partner for hospitals running a da Vinci robotic surgery program.   Based on its expertise, this role focuses on identifies and tailors the nature and extent of staff in-servicing, day-to-day program execution, technology onboarding and operational support, communicating identified needs to hospital OR operations and leadership. The DVS will work alongside the da Vinci Clinical Sales Representative .
Essential Job Duties
Collaboration & Field Partnership (Within a CSM Team)
Partner with the local CSR/CSM and cross-functional business partners to create, own, scale and execute best practices and deployment of ecosystem resources.
Lead account support plans that drive safe program execution and increase customer autonomy over time, including setting objectives, timelines and resources for relevant customers, in consultation with CSR/CSM.
Identify, solicit and provide field feedback and customer insights to internal teams to improve training, support resources, and customer experience.
Support adoption of digital solutions by helping customers build comfort and capability through in-servicing and troubleshooting.
Clinical & Technical Support
Identify and provide on-site, non-scrubbed operating room support for procedures utilizing the da Vinci Surgical System and associated technologies.
Support OR teams with room readiness and procedural workflow, including system setup support, docking workflow support, and intraoperative troubleshooting.
Serve as a clinical product expert to help ensure optimal, safe system use and adherence to applicable IFUs, hospital policies, and safety protocols.
Motivate and support adoption of advanced instruments and accessories by ensuring teams understand proper setup, handling, and intended use.
Partner with and promote consistent readiness and workflow by supporting day-to-day execution of the robotic program, coordinating with OR leadership, nursing, SPD/sterile processing, and biomedical teams.
Assist with operational support activities such as facilitating appropriate internal handoffs for service needs.
Ensure the right stakeholders are aligned (OR, SPD, biomed, IT) for successful day-to-day operation and new technology onboarding to help reduce friction.
Maintain accurate internal documentation of support activities per company process (e.g., case support notes, training records, service/escalation tracking).
Training & Education (Care Team Enablement)
Determine the need for, customize and deliver customer-specific hands-on training and in-services to nurses, surgical technologists, SPD teams, and other care team members on safe and effective use of da Vinci platforms and associated technologies.
Support onboarding and education for new users through structured training touchpoints (e.g., new staff orientation, refresher training, workflow standardization).
Lead new site start-ups by identifying and delivering onboarding programs and coordinating training logistics with the CSR/CSM and hospital stakeholders.
Support new technology installs by coordinating readiness activities and providing post-install education to care teams.
Act as a resource for ongoing education, product updates, and workflow optimization.
Escalation & Customer Issue Management
Analyze and leverage utilization, turnover, and other relevant case data to recommend operational changes to customers
Provide first-line support and expertise for common setup and workflow issues during live cases and training sessions.
Identify, resolve and where necessary escalate issues appropriately to internal partners (e.g., Technical Support, Field Service, Clinical/Medical counterparts).
Market & Clinical Insights
Collect and communicate customer feedback and experiences to clinical counterparts and internal business partners.  Prioritizing, distilling and reporting relevant customer feedback, in real time.
Stay up to date on clinical literature, competitive products, and evolving treatment guidelines.
Assist in clinical trial support when required.
Assist in field action activities when necessary.
Required Skills and Experience
Experience: 2+ years in an operating room-related role
Clinical experience is preferred.
Experience as a robotics coordinator, surgical assistant, and/or surgical nurse plus industry experience strongly preferred.
Understanding of soft tissue anatomy & procedures.
Exhibit a working knowledge of typical hospital policies.
Excellent communication, teaching, and interpersonal skills.
Strong problem solving and troubleshooting skills.
Ability to work in high-pressure environments (managing multiple ORs) and coordination of multiple tasks at one time.
Adaptability to evolving technologies and complex procedures.
Team oriented with a commercial mindset.
Willingness to travel up to 40%. Primary travel will be within a CSM team.
Ability to travel within a Clinical Sales Manager team geography, supporting multiple hospitals.
Flexibility to support early starts, after-hours cases, and weekend procedures based on customer need and territory utilization.
Required Education and Training
Associates degree. Bachelor’s degree preferred.
Degrees in (RN, PA, NP, RT, or other clinical credentials) are welcomed.
Working Conditions
Ability to stand for extended periods and provide in-person case support within an operating room (OR) environment, which includes pushing, pulling, lifting and squatting.

Collaboration & Field Partnership (Within a CSM Team)
Partner with the local CSR/CSM and cross-functional business partners to create, own, scale and execute best practices and deployment of ecosystem resources.

Identify, solicit and provide field feedback and customer insights to internal teams to improve training, support resources, and customer experience.
Support adoption of digital solutions by helping customers build comfort and capability through in-servicing and troubleshooting.
Clinical & Technical Support
Identify and provide on-site, non-scrubbed operating room support for procedures utilizing the da Vinci Surgical System and associated technologies.
Support OR teams with room readiness and procedural workflow, including system setup support, docking workflow support, and intraoperative troubleshooting.
Serve as a clinical product expert to help ensure optimal, safe system use and adherence to applicable IFUs, hospital policies, and safety protocols.
Motivate and support adoption of advanced instruments and accessories by ensuring teams understand proper setup, handling, and intended use.
Partner with and promote consistent readiness and workflow by supporting day-to-day execution of the robotic program, coordinating with OR leadership, nursing, SPD/sterile processing, and biomedical teams.
Assist with operational support activities such as facilitating appropriate internal handoffs for service needs.
Ensure the right stakeholders are aligned (OR, SPD, biomed, IT) for successful day-to-day operation and new technology onboarding to help reduce friction.
Maintain accurate internal documentation of support activities per company process (e.g., case support notes, training records, service/escalation tracking).

Determine the need for, customize and deliver customer-specific hands-on training and in-services to nurses, surgical technologists, SPD teams, and other care team members on safe and effective use of da Vinci platforms and associated technologies.
Support onboarding and education for new users through structured training touchpoints (e.g., new staff orientation, refresher training, workflow standardization).
Lead new site start-ups by identifying and delivering onboarding programs and coordinating training logistics with the CSR/CSM and hospital stakeholders.

As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care, our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion—have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare, you’ll find your purpose here.
*Please note: Candidates must live within or be willing to relocate to the Louisville, KY Area to perform the duties of this role.
Primary Function of Position
The DaVinci Specialist (DVS) will provide expert clinical & technical support, build, customize and coordinate education & training to physicians, nurses, and hospital staff on the use of DaVinci surgery, devices and therapies. This role partners closely with the sales team, specifically the Clinical Sales Representative and Clinical Sales Manager, to ensure safe and effective product adoption and quality control while driving positive patient outcomes.
The DaVinci Specialist is a dedicated program execution & clinical education partner for hospitals running a da Vinci robotic surgery program.   Based on its expertise, this role focuses on identifies and tailors the nature and extent of staff in-servicing, day-to-day program execution, technology onboarding and operational support, communicating identified needs to hospital OR operations and leadership. The DVS will work alongside the daVinci Clinical Sales Representative .
Essential Job Duties
Collaboration & Field Partnership (Within a CSM Team)
Partner with the local CSR/CSM and cross-functional business partners to create, own, scale and execute best practices and deployment of ecosystem resources.
Lead account support plans that drive safe program execution and increase customer autonomy over time, including setting objectives, timelines and resources for relevant customers, in consultation with CSR/CSM.
Identify, solicit and provide field feedback and customer insights to internal teams to improve training, support resources, and customer experience.
Support adoption of digital solutions by helping customers build comfort and capability through in-servicing and troubleshooting.
Clinical & Technical Support
Identify and provide on-site, non-scrubbed operating room support for procedures utilizing the da Vinci Surgical System and associated technologies.
Support OR teams with room readiness and procedural workflow, including system setup support, docking workflow support, and intraoperative troubleshooting.
Serve as a clinical product expert to help ensure optimal, safe system use and adherence to applicable IFUs, hospital policies, and safety protocols.
Motivate and support adoption of advanced instruments and accessories by ensuring teams understand proper setup, handling, and intended use.
Partner with and promote consistent readiness and workflow by supporting day-to-day execution of the robotic program, coordinating with OR leadership, nursing, SPD/sterile processing, and biomedical teams.
Assist with operational support activities such as facilitating appropriate internal handoffs for service needs.
Ensure the right stakeholders are aligned (OR, SPD, biomed, IT) for successful day-to-day operation and new technology onboarding to help reduce friction.
Maintain accurate internal documentation of support activities per company process (e.g., case support notes, training records, service/escalation tracking).
Training & Education (Care Team Enablement)
Determine the need for, customize and deliver customer-specific hands-on training and in-services to nurses, surgical technologists, SPD teams, and other care team members on safe and effective use of da Vinci platforms and associated technologies.
Support onboarding and education for new users through structured training touchpoints (e.g., new staff orientation, refresher training, workflow standardization).
Lead new site start-ups by identifying and delivering onboarding programs and coordinating training logistics with the CSR/CSM and hospital stakeholders.
Support new technology installs by coordinating readiness activities and providing post-install education to care teams.
Act as a resource for ongoing education, product updates, and workflow optimization.
Escalation & Customer Issue Management
Analyze and leverage utilization, turnover, and other relevant case data to recommend operational changes to customers
Provide first-line support and expertise for common setup and workflow issues during live cases and training sessions.
Identify, resolve and where necessary escalate issues appropriately to internal partners (e.g., Technical Support, Field Service, Clinical/Medical counterparts).
Market & Clinical Insights
Collect and communicate customer feedback and experiences to clinical counterparts and internal business partners.  Prioritizing, distilling and reporting relevant customer feedback, in real time.
Stay up to date on clinical literature, competitive products, and evolving treatment guidelines.
Assist in clinical trial support when required.
Assist in field action activities when necessary.
Required Skills and Experience
Experience: 2+ years in an operating room-related role
Clinical experience is preferred.
Experience as a robotics coordinator, surgical assistant, and/or surgical nurse plus industry experience strongly preferred.
Understanding of soft tissue anatomy & procedures.
Exhibit a working knowledge of typical hospital policies.
Excellent communication, teaching, and interpersonal skills.
Strong problem solving and troubleshooting skills.
Ability to work in high-pressure environments (managing multiple ORs) and coordination of multiple tasks at one time.
Adaptability to evolving technologies and complex procedures.
Team oriented with a commercial mindset.
Willingness to travel up to 40%. Primary travel will be within a CSM team.
Ability to travel within a Clinical Sales Manager team geography, supporting multiple hospitals.
Flexibility to support early starts, after-hours cases, and weekend procedures based on customer need and territory utilization.
Required Education and Training
Associates degree. Bachelor’s degree preferred.
Degrees in (RN, PA, NP, RT, or other clinical credentials) are welcomed.
Working Conditions
Ability to stand for extended periods and provide in-person case support within an operating room (OR) environment, which includes pushing, pulling, lifting and squatting.

Lead architecture, configuration, and governance of Windows and macOS endpoint environments.

Lead endpoint-related projects, upgrades, and process improvements

Demonstrated ability to lead technical initiatives and resolve complex issues.
Excellent communication, documentation, and customer service skills.
Ability to travel domestically/internationally as needed; participation in on-call rotation required.
Eligible to work in the United States without the need for employer visa sponsorship now or in the future

Strong background supporting Azure Virtual Desktop, Citrix, or other DaaS platforms.
Experience with modern device management and zero‑touch deployment strategies.

Relevant certifications (Microsoft, CompTIA, ITIL).
Experience coaching or mentoring team members.
Fluent in English; Spanish proficiency a plus.
Key Competencies
Strong analytical and troubleshooting skills.
Ability to lead projects and drive process improvements.
Customer-focused mindset.
Organized, detail-oriented, and capable of prioritizing multiple initiatives.

Take advantage of opportunities for skill development in GIS software, scripting, and renewable energy workflows.

Proficiency with ESRI software (ArcGIS Pro, ArcGIS Online / ArcGIS E nterprise ).
Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
Ability to communicate clearly and work as part of a team.
Eligible to work in the United States without the need for employer visa sponsorship now or in the future.

We are hiring for multiple product development roles providing direction for and execution of projects across our North America R&D teams. The Kraft Heinz Company is one of the largest food and beverage companies in the world, with eight $1 billion+ brands and global sales of approximately $25 billion. title: Food Safety Associate
location: Massillon - Hourly, Ohio, United States of America
description:
Hourly manufacturing position
Job Description
Job Summary/Purpose:
This position provides the front line of quality assurance activity.  The principle objective is to observe and audit the processes of production and verify that our various requirements are being met.
Starting wage $25.72
Essential Responsibilities
·         Participate/support the RMP (Risk Management Process) and assist in the development of the system and operational standards and corrective actions.
·         Required to gain working knowledge in Company policy in regards to Quality and Food Safety.
·         Audit and record HACCP's and control points data as required by policy.
·         Audit and record ingredients use for verification of lot tracking capabilities using process sheets, weight sheets and other product specification data.
·         Audit processing systems for conformity to company standards and specifications and Government Regulations.
·         Apply Hold Tags to / for equipment, product or areas audited found to be out of compliance.
·         Document / Log the information about Hold Tags applied and generate components reject, and Hold Report.
·         Audit and record operational sanitation activities and GMP’s in assigned area.
·         Audit weight control records for assigned lines.
·         Audit information on all product cartons and cases, including product description, codes and date for assigned areas.
·         Monitor product quality through informal and formal procedures as required on all assigned products / lines.
·         Assist training of others in traditional Quality Assurance functions as needed.
·         Collect required PE/NLV/Micro/Fat, etc. samples for assigned areas.
·         Perform Product Evaluations as specified in corporate SOP’s and data entry and maintain FM log.
·         Evaluate and analyze products rejected by metal detector from assigned lines.
·         Perform metal detector and check weigher verification checks for accuracy during operations.
·         Monitor and maintain inventory of grading and lab supplies, forms, etc.
·         Maintain Production log book using the current pack-plans.
·         Responsible for collection, sorting, electronically scanning and filing all production process sheets.
·         Perform 5S housekeeping duties in the lab area as necessary.
·         Working knowledge of Oracl Agile.
·         Issue process sheet to files for production use daily, issue changes if pack plan changes warrant.
·         Monitoring rework/hold, and assist in disposition.
·         Inform and assist supervisors and team leaders to take corrective action in quality issues, GMP, SOP, HACCP/Formulation.
·         Collect necessary information to help complete SCAR process.
·         Backup Micro Technician:
Conducts and records micro testing on ingredients, finished product, equipment & environment
Perform standard & AOAC approved method microbiological tests & analysis for total plate count
Perform routine and scheduled tests and analysis of air and environmental conditions
Place all non-compliant product on “Hold” & maintain “Hold” lists.
Purchasing and maintaining inventories of all equipment/chemicals used in QA
Files & maintain completed QA paperwork
Conducts lab audits & assist in reviewing/updating Microbiological S.O.P.
Reports all non-compliance analyses to QA Supervisor, daily
As necessary, other duties and/or projects may be assigned
·         Training and Safety – Provide a safe and healthful work environment for all personnel through consistent support of the company’s Heinz Safety Process.  Oversee safety processes including, but not limited to, goal setting, hazard recognition, and elimination, administration of safety procedures and corresponding corrective action, area inspection, job skills, and compliance training, accident investigation and safety meetings.
·         Interprets company policies to workers and enforces policies and safety regulations.
·         Must be able to work flexible hours; days, afternoons, midnights, overtime and weekends as necessary.
·         As necessary, other duties and/or projects may be assigned.
Education and Experience
·         BS Degree for Microbiology, Biology, Chemistry or other related Science, Preferred.  High school diploma or general education degree (GED); two to four years related experience and/or training; or a combination of related education and related work experience.
·         Comprehensive knowledge of PC’s, scales, refractometer, ovens and other office equipment.
·         Comprehensive knowledge of manufacturing environment.
·         Comprehensive knowledge of the Code of Federal Regulations that deal specifically with food, meat and poultry.
·         Comprehensive knowledge of the OSHA requirements for the job assigned.
Skills, Knowledge and Abilities
·         Ability to detect quality errors or problems and take corrective action within assigned scope of authority.
·         Reading, comprehension and math skills required.
·         Demonstrate reliability and good work ethics, quality work performance, attention to detail is a must, and maintain a good working relationship with all other departments.
·         Must be able to work independently with little supervision.
·         Ability to multitask and work in a team oriented fast-paced environment.
·         Excellent interpersonal, and organizational skills and must be detail and process oriented.
·         Must have the ability to exercise considerable judgment and be able to identify and solve problems.
·         Must have excellent written and verbal communication skills.
·         Must have basic computer skills.
·         Proficient computer skills in Excel and/or Access, Word, e-mail.
·         Ability to define problems, collect data, establish facts, and draw valid conclusions.
·         Must be able to work independently with little supervision.
·         Must be able to work any shift and overtime, including weekends.
Physical/Mental Requirements
·         Ability to stand, walk, sit, climb, balance, stoop, kneel, crouch and crawl.
·         Ability to use hands/arms to reach, handle, or feel objects, tools or controls.
·         Ability to work in all areas of the facility including hot and cold areas, and be exposed to wet and humid conditions.
·         Must be able to lift and or move up to 50 lbs or more.
·         Must have excellent vision, distant and peripheral, with the ability to identify and distinguish items.
·         The noise level in the work environment is usually high, and ear protection is required.
·         May work near moving mechanical parts, high and/or confining places and in outside weather conditions.
About Us
Kraft Heinz is a global food company with a delicious heritage. With iconic and emerging food and beverage brands around the world, we deliver the best taste, fun and quality to every meal table we touch. We’re on a mission to disrupt not only our own business, but the global food industry. A consumer obsession and unexpected partnerships fuel our progress as we drive innovation across every part of our company.

description:
As the Principal Engineer, Packaging Materials & Performance, you will lead the development and deployment of packaging performance requirements across the Kraft Heinz North America portfolio. The primary purpose of this role is to define the material, package, manufacturing, sustainability, and consumer performance requirements that enable successful packaging development, commercialization, and long-term business performance. These requirements will guide packaging design decisions, supplier alignment, technical validation, and commercialization activities across a diverse portfolio of packaging formats and technologies.
Success in this role requires strong cross-functional collaboration, strategic influence, prioritization, technical problem solving, thoughtful people development, and the ability to lead multiple complex initiatives simultaneously. Working closely with Packaging R&D, Innovation, Platform and Process Packaging, Quality, Operations, Procurement, and external partners, you will establish the technical foundation that ensures packaging systems meet functional, quality, shelf-life, manufacturing, consumer experience, sustainability, and regulatory expectations. Performance specifications are a key output of this work, but the role is fundamentally focused on technical packaging leadership, material performance understanding, and requirement development rather than specification administration. This position also provides leadership for packaging sustainability compliance activities, including support of Extended Producer Responsibility requirements and emerging packaging regulations.
Essential Functions & Responsibilities Lead packaging performance requirements. Define enterprise requirements for packaging materials, package systems, and packaging technologies across the portfolio.
Serve as a technical authority. Provide expertise in barrier properties, mechanical performance, seal integrity, distribution durability, compatibility, machinability, sustainability performance, and consumer use.
Translate needs into measurable criteria. Convert product, consumer, operational, supply chain, sustainability, regulatory, and business needs into clear performance targets and technical acceptance requirements.
Guide material and design decisions. Establish performance targets that inform package development, material selection, supplier engagement, and commercialization choices.
Define and execute validation. Establish testing methods, validation strategies, and acceptance criteria required to demonstrate package performance. Design and oversee packaging validation activities including laboratory testing, pilot plant evaluations, manufacturing trials, distribution testing, and commercial production startup support.
Manage technical risk. Identify, assess, and mitigate risks related to packaging materials, structures, manufacturing processes, and package performance.
Enable commercialization. Build performance verification plans that support concept development, proof of concept, scale-up, launch, and ongoing product support.
Solve complex performance problems. Use scientific and engineering principles, experimental design, and data analysis to investigate failures, close performance gaps, and reduce commercialization risk.
Build organizational capability. Develop tools, training, and coaching that strengthen performance-based packaging development and technical requirement definition.
Build technical capability. Coach and mentor team members in packaging materials, package performance, validation methodologies, commercialization, and technical problem solving. Provide technical leadership and mentorship to cross-functional packaging teams and project stakeholders.
Measure effectiveness. Track outcomes such as commercialization success, reduced rework, improved launch readiness, fewer late-stage changes, and stronger package performance.
Maintain requirement governance. Ensure performance requirements are measurable, technically justified, current, approved, and communicated through effective documentation and change-control practices.
Key Outputs & Deliverables Enterprise packaging performance standards and requirements.
Material and package-system performance criteria for major packaging platforms.
Validation strategies, testing methodologies, and technical acceptance criteria.
Project-ready performance requirements that support innovation, productivity, quality, sustainability, and commercialization objectives.
Technical risk assessments and mitigation plans for packaging systems and material technologies.
Governed performance-requirement documentation that enables clear communication, supplier alignment, and consistent execution.
Training materials, tools, and resources that strengthen packaging development practices across the organization.
Expected Experience & Required Skills

As a Research Lead on the End-to-End (E2E) Complex Projects team, you will serve as a deep technical processing expert responsible for hands-on execution of complex, high-impact processing projects from concept through commercialization. Execute end-to-end technical delivery across assigned complex processing projects, including technical briefing, concept development, technical design, learning plans, pilot runs, capital design, and commercialization handover to Operations/Supply Chain.

Support cost optimization and value engineering efforts that improve margin, sustainability, and reinvestment priorities.

Deliver successful technical execution across concurrent complex processing projects within innovation and platform portfolios, meeting committed timelines, budgets, and technical performance targets.

Job Description
Job Purpose
​​As the Packaging Materials Senior Manager within the Sustainability & Materials Center of Excellence, you will lead a team of technical experts charged with developing plastic packaging solutions, across both rigids and flexibles to serve the North American portfolio. The objective of the team is to develop material and format solutions that meet sustainability requirements, addressing innovation, compliance, and value engineering initiatives. The team will develop and lead technical strategies and deliver novel, functional, cost-competitive solutions. In this role you will partner with Innovation, Process, and Platform packaging teams as well as cross-functional stakeholders to translate technical and sustainability requirements into viable, commercial, manufacturable solutions. The role includes leading the team to identify material/polymer/packaging technology solutions and research pathways, and leading proof of concept, technology scale-up, and seamless transition of technologies to the business units. The ideal candidate combines deep technical packaging expertise with strong sustainability knowledge and proven experience managing complex projects and technical teams. ​     Essential Functions & Responsibilities    ​​Lead and prioritize a portfolio of complex plastic packaging technology strategies and initiatives, including balancing technology exploration with proof of concept of novel technologies and managing complex partnerships across the value chain, demonstrating value and business case for technology applications.
​Build, coordinate and manage relationships and partnerships with suppliers and technology providers (e.g., resin, coating and other material suppliers and packaging manufacturers) and external partners (e.g., universities, institutes, start-ups, open innovation networks).
​Identify material/polymer/packaging technology solutions that avoid material bans and regulatory risks.
​Advance recyclable, reusable, and compliant plastic packaging formats aligned with enterprise sustainability goals and legislative requirements.
​Deliver packaging designs to  Performance-Based Specifications (PBS) , ensuring solutions meet defined functionality, quality, shelf-life, consumer experience, and manufacturing performance outcomes (rather than prescriptive designs).
​Provide technical leadership and oversight on packaging reviews, ensuring design decisions align with enterprise standards, manufacturability, sustainability, and long-term platform strategy.
​Own project and portfolio-level budgets, resourcing strategies and capacity planning, ensuring delivery within approved financial guardrails; develop and maintain project plans, schedules, budgets, and resource allocations; monitor progress, assess risk, and proactively escalate tradeoffs.
​Serve as an accountable owner for governance, escalation and go/no-go decisions; represent packaging steering forums and influence stakeholders.
​Act as technical expert for junior developers and direct team to flex onto projects requiring problem solving.
​Partner with legal to build robust IP strategies; conduct exploration to build an IP portfolio to drive competitive advantage.
​Mentor, coach and train junior project team members and contribute to PMO best practices and templates.
​Build and sustain a high-performing technical team; manage, coach, mentor and retain employees, including goal setting, performance management, salary planning and hiring.
​Build strong succession and upskilling plans for junior talent, maximizing apprenticeship with more senior/experienced team members.​
People Management Responsibilities   Team (salaried): targeting 3 direct reports
Key Outputs & Deliverables    Deliver technology strategy and prioritize a portfolio of complex plastic packaging technology/format initiatives to deliver against sustainability, innovation and value engineering initiatives.
Lead and deploy a team of packaging technical experts to deliver 7 to 10 concurrent complex packaging technology projects annually, meeting committed timelines, budgets, and technical performance targets from concept through proof of concept and handover.
Ensure full compliance with evolving sustainability and regulatory requirements for portfolio projects, including:
Minimizing Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) fees
Designing packaging solutions that avoid material bans and regulatory risks
Advancing recyclable, reusable, and compliant packaging formats aligned with enterprise sustainability goals and legislative requirements
Deliver packaging designs to PBS, ensuring solutions meet defined functional, quality, shelf-life, consumer experience, and manufacturing performance outcomes.
Expected Experience & Required Skills   ​​BS/MS/PhD degree in Engineering, Materials, Chemical or Packaging Engineering preferred or related discipline.
​Minimum 8 years of R&D technology development and commercialization experience in packaging and project leadership experience (consumer goods, food & beverage, pharma or similar preferred).
​Demonstrated experience managing end-to-end development projects, identifying and driving packaging technology initiatives, leading external partnerships, and coordinating cross-functional teams.
​Demonstrated experience in people management
​Strong technical knowledge of  materials  (polymers, coatings and additives, etc.) and  manufacturing constraints including converting processes (e.g., forming, filling, labeling, injection molding, blow molding, thermoforming, extrusion, lamination), bottle closure and dispensing systems.
​Proven project management/PMO skills; experience with governance, risk management, budget management, and stakeholder reporting.
​Expert knowledge of design of experiments and statistics; strong technical problem solving.
​Excellent communication, negotiation and interpersonal skills; ability to influence at all levels.
​Previous experience leading complex, multisite or global packaging or technology launches.
​Expert knowledge of sustainable packaging solutions, material/package industry standards and regulations.
​Experience with pilot line setups and scale-up to industrial production.
​Willingness and ability to travel up to 25% of the time.​

The Assistant General Counsel, Sustainability (Human Rights & Supply Chain Due Diligence) will play a senior role on the enterprise-level Sustainability Legal team at Mars, Inc. This role serves as the global legal lead for business and human rights and supply chain due diligence within Mars.
This is a high-visibility role in a small headquarters team. The role acts as a subject-matter lead within the enterprise Sustainability Legal framework, setting legal strategy, guardrails, governance approaches, and escalation protocols for human-rights-related risks and regulations. The successful candidate will be a senior, independent lawyer who can influence without authority, build trust across a complex global organization, and provide clear, practical advice in a rapidly evolving regulatory environment.
What will be your key responsibilities?
Provide senior legal advice on global business and human rights, responsible sourcing, and supply chain due diligence issues affecting Mars across segments, regions, and functions.
Lead enterprise legal strategy for human-rights and supply-chain-due-diligence-related regulations and legal risks, including enterprise interpretation, legal guardrails, governance frameworks, and escalation protocols.
Serve as the subject-matter lead for human rights within Mars’ enterprise Sustainability Legal framework and help shape a One-Mars legal approach in this area.
Lead or support legal workstreams relating to material sustainability regulations in the role’s subject-matter area, including the CSRD, CS3D, LkSG, EUDR, FLR and other forced labor and responsible sourcing regulations and related emerging global developments.
Support high-risk issues, investigations, and escalations relating to business and human rights, responsible sourcing, and supply chain due diligence matters.

Partner closely with segment and regional legal teams to align on enterprise legal positions, promote consistent application of human rights legal standards and due diligence requirements, and enable local operationalization without displacing segment or regional ownership.
Act as a trusted connector among Legal, Sustainability, Procurement, Finance, and Corporate and Public Affairs at the corporate, segment, and regional levels to promote consistent, practical, and risk-balanced legal approaches across Mars.
Advise Public Affairs and other corporate stakeholders on legal considerations arising from sustainability-related policy development, advocacy positions, external engagement, and participation in industry or multistakeholder forums where human rights or supply chain due diligence issues are implicated.
Support legal trend analysis and regulatory insights for emerging business and human rights, responsible sourcing, and supply chain due diligence laws, enforcement trends, and stakeholder expectations.
Develop and deliver training and capacity-building for legal and business stakeholders on human rights and supply chain due diligence legal risk and compliance requirements.
What are we looking for?
Law degree from an accredited university in the U.S., EU, UK, or another relevant jurisdiction.
Licensed, admitted, or otherwise qualified to practice law in at least one relevant jurisdiction.
12 to 15+ years of relevant legal experience, including significant experience advising on business and human rights, responsible sourcing, supply chain due diligence, forced labor, sustainability compliance, or related regulatory matters.
Deep knowledge of business and human rights frameworks, emerging due diligence regulations, forced labor laws, responsible sourcing programs, and human rights risk management.
Demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively across adjacent sustainability legal topics, for example sustainability claims, deforestation, reporting, packaging, or other emerging regulatory issues, as part of an integrated enterprise sustainability legal model.
Experience working in-house at a global organization preferred, particularly in a matrixed environment involving corporate, segment, regional, and functional stakeholders.
Experience handling sensitive, high-risk issues, investigations, or escalations involving human rights, responsible sourcing, or supply chain due diligence matters.
Familiarity with public policy development, advocacy, or external affairs processes, including experience advising Public Affairs, Government Relations or similar teams on legal and reputational considerations related to sustainability policy matters.
Strong judgment, communication, influencing, and stakeholder-management skills, with the ability to provide practical, risk-balanced advice to senior legal and business leaders.
Demonstrated ability to build alignment across functions and geographies without relying solely on formal authority.
Ability to establish and maintain clear role boundaries, clarify ownership across center, segment, and regional teams, and escalate issues appropriately while preserving collaborative relationships.

The role also provides training and guidance to site associates to support on-line sensory programs and works in partnership with BU/Global Sensory Scientists to implement site-specific innovations that strengthen product quality, consistency, and conformance. Strong computer skills
Flexibility to work overtime as needed

title: Shift Manager (Nights)
description:
Job Description:
SUMMARY
The Shift Manager is a front-line operations leader responsible for improving Quality, Human Safety, and Product Cost Efficiency while engaging and developing talent. This role leads teams of 25-30 production associates, ensuring operational targets are met. The Shift Manager focuses on safety, quality, performance management, continuous improvement, and associate development for their assigned area. They collaborate with the 24-hour Area Leadership Team to implement continuous improvement strategies and Supply Excellence initiatives. This leader is also responsible for building and managing an effective team, ensuring proper training, and enforcing policies.
ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Production Efficiency: Lead multi-line teams to efficiently convert materials into quality products in a safe, sanitary manner, meeting product design specifications.
Change Management: Implement and recommend changes in methods, equipment, or systems to achieve operational goals using a Continuous Improvement mindset.
Supply Excellence (SE): Lead or support SE Pillars, including Autonomous Maintenance (AM) and Autonomous Work Teams (AWTs), ensuring accuracy in reliability data collection.
Nature’s Bakery Operating System: Advocate for and support the site's Daily Management System, coaching teams in the Value Stream Operating System.
Area Ownership: Collaborate with the Area Leadership Team to create and execute a reliability strategy for your area.
Coaching: Develop operators’ functional and leadership skills while driving accountability in safety, quality, and team engagement.
Operations Coordination: Manage materials, staffing, and resources to support line operations and changeovers.
Standards Implementation: Ensure standards are communicated, reinforced, and adhered to through coaching and accountability.
Safety and Quality: Drive a strong focus on safety and food safety, ensuring the ongoing production of safe, defect-free products. HACCP proficiency is required.
Associate Development: Manage associate relations, recruitment, training, and development, fostering a high-engagement team environment.
Performance Management: Set performance goals, measure progress, and take corrective action as needed.
Troubleshooting: Lead preventive maintenance and equipment troubleshooting efforts to achieve desired performance.
Escalations: Identify risks and resolve escalated issues on-shift, assigning resources as necessary.
Communication and Engagement: Ensure open communication and foster an environment of high associate engagement.
Technological Advancement: Identify opportunities for technological improvements to enhance line performance.
Strategy Implementation: Help implement strategies to drive near-term operational improvements.
Recruitment and Onboarding: Partner with Talent Acquisition to recruit, select, and onboard associates for operational roles.
EXPERIENCE
Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience (4+ years in a technical manufacturing continuous improvement environment with a High School Diploma).
Prior experience leading manufacturing teams for 4+ years with high preference for direct report responsibility leading larger production teams
Demonstrated leadership experience, preferably with direct people management.
Knowledge of Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) and plant operations.
Strong communication skills and the ability to collaborate across all functions.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, etc.)
Experience with plant sanitation practices and OSHA safety standards or certifications.
HACCP proficiency is required; this manager owns ongoing training and championing of quality goals and improvements at the Area Shift level.
Ability to deliver performance feedback and hold associates accountable to business objectives.

Normal visual acuity (near, far and peripheral with correction), defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria. Documents completed work using approved tools and procedural templates for more experienced technician review. Completes and provides coaching to support less experienced technicians for mandatory, technical, and procedural training assignments. Analyzes findings from reports and documents observations.

Determines when troubleshooting efforts are deemed adequate and communicates or escalates to suppliers, engineers, or more experienced colleagues as needed. Has a hands-on understanding of how equipment works within disciplines they have been trained and how to troubleshoot to a subsystem level. Provides consultation to less experienced colleagues with troubleshooting systems and problems. May lead efforts to troubleshoot issues and identify root causes.

Tracks hours for performed tasks within applicable task management systems. Adds required data, documents, logs changes, and upkeeps procedures related to building management systems and reports. Properly signals spare equipment and parts utilization within maintenance work orders.
Works on advanced tasks (e.g., vendor contact, escalations) independently. Serves as a subject matter expert in critical environments-related systems within the data center, and advises less experienced colleagues on such topics. Possesses an understanding of and operates equipment and systems within a set discipline (e.g., electrical, mechanical, controls) with knowledge of the interactions between them and overall operation of a data center. Operates all systems and equipment in a safe and professional manner.
Inspects and supervises critical environment-related facility equipment (e.g., controls, heating, ventilation, and air conditioning [HVAC], mechanical systems), building, and grounds for unsafe or abnormal conditions to develop and analyze trends. Understands critical system alarms for single discipline(s) of equipment, their meanings, and engages with appropriate escalation processes or procedures. Recognizes circumstances where execution would be considered safe to proceed. Performs various inspections and validations of equipment performance. Monitors the performance from central monitoring locations (i.e., Facility Operations Centers) of maintenance and operations of equipment (e.g., electrical, mechanical, fire/life safety) within the data center. Escalates per applicable policies and standards. Utilizes telemetry, control systems, and other platforms to monitor site status, analyze past and current events, as well as other processes, and can identify all alarms. Uses technical expertise, prior experience, and device analytics to recognize trends with equipment behavior and checks potential issues as they arise. Advises less experienced colleagues on issues found while monitoring applicable CE systems. Performs all monitoring equipment repair, replacement, and maintenance work, which meets or exceeds Microsoft Service Level Agreement (SLA) requirements.
Safety and quickly responds to and leads an onsite incident response team for all abnormal conditions that impact operations, and coordinates with other critical facilities professionals to perform corrective repairs, without supervision. Gathers necessary information and creates incident timelines/data, root-cause analyses, and/or action items following an abnormal condition as required. title: Director of Datacenter IT Operations
description:
Overview
Microsoft's Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) is the engine that powers our cloud services. It delivers the core infrastructure and foundational technologies for Microsoft's online services, including Bing, Microsoft 365, Xbox, OneDrive and the Microsoft Azure platform. Our infrastructure is a global portfolio of more than 200 datacenters in 32 countries and millions of servers. It supports more than 1 billion customers and 20 million businesses in over 90 countries.
Reporting to the Charlotte Metro Director, the Director of Datacenter IT Operations is the senior IT Operations leader for the Charlotte Metro. This leader owns end-to-end IT operations, IT outfitting and IT infrastructure delivery across all Class A and Class B datacenter facilities in the metro. That organization is accountable for safe, secure, on-time and defect-free delivery of customer capacity, and for reliable, SLA-compliant operation of IT infrastructure once it is live.
The role covers the full IT lifecycle. That starts with design input and construction coordination, continues through IT outfitting, network and server deployment, operational readiness and turnover, and extends into steady-state operations, hardware lifecycle management and decommissioning. The Director partners closely with Critical Environment (CE), IAM/Logistics, Datacenter Delivery (DCD), Datacenter Engineering (DCE), Commissioning, network and hardware engineering teams, and vendors. Together they ensure IT requirements are built in from the start and that Operations is ready to take ownership on Day 1.
Success in this role requires strong organizational leadership, disciplined service management, financial acumen, and the ability to turn technical and operational risk into clear, decision-ready recommendations for metro, regional and CO+I leadership. With environmental sustainability and optimization at the forefront of our datacenter design and operations, we continue to grow and evolve to meet the business demands that make Microsoft a world-class cloud provider.
Do you want to empower billions across the world? Come and join us in CO+I and be at the forefront of the action!
Responsibilities
Organizational Leadership and People Management
Build, lead, coach and develop the Charlotte Metro IT Operations organization, including Datacenter Technician Managers, Datacenter Program Managers and Datacenter Technicians across all Class A and Class B facilities.
Deliver success through empowerment and accountability by modeling, coaching and caring. Live our culture, embody our values and practice our leadership principles.
Set the IT organization's strategy, priorities, operating rhythm, performance expectations and long-term capability roadmap in line with metro and CO+I priorities.
Lead IT workforce, capacity and succession planning across the metro. Allocate resources across campuses and sites based on business priority, infrastructure complexity, operational risk and future demand.
Attract, hire and retain great people. Know everyone's capabilities and aspirations, invest in the growth of others, and develop the next generation of leaders through intentional delegation and succession planning.
Make sure teams complete required training and certifications. Partner with Learning & Development to evolve the training portfolio as technology and site requirements change.
Recognize team successes and reward teamwork while keeping the culture focused on strategic goals.
2. IT Operations and Service Delivery
Own end-to-end service compliance, quality and client satisfaction for all IT services in the metro, against agreed SLAs, OLAs, KPIs and OKRs.
Oversee all IT operations activity, including server and rack deployment, network turn-up, structured cabling, break-fix and hardware repair, asset tracking, decommissions, and secure media handling and destruction.
Apply deep subject-matter expertise and escalate as needed to meet SLA/OLA commitments with minimal disruption to customers and the business. Review metrics with leaders so everyone understands targets and current performance.
Manage relationships with internal clients and service-line partners so expectations are clear and understood, and deliver solutions with a strong customer focus.
Understand future business demand in each facility so that IT staffing, tooling, spares and resources keep pace with growth.
Share common and recurring issues with regional and global teams, and promote best practices that prevent recurrence and make resolution more efficient.
3. IT Outfitting, Capacity Delivery and Operational Readiness
Own IT outfitting and infrastructure delivery for new builds, expansions, retrofits and live-site changes across all Class A and Class B facilities in the metro.
Make sure IT requirements are built into infrastructure designs and formal design reviews, including network, structured cabling, rack/enclosure layouts, power distribution to IT, maintainability, security and supportability.
Keep IT Operations engaged throughout construction and commissioning, including quality reviews, readiness assessments, commissioning participation and resolution of IT concerns before turnover.
Make sure documentation, procedures, spares, tooling, systems access, training and operational dependencies are in place before operational acceptance, so IT teams can safely and effectively take ownership on Day 1.
Support Go/No-Go and readiness decisions with clear, data-driven assessments of IT infrastructure and operational risk.
Ensure on-time, defect-free delivery of customer capacity within SLA commitments. Govern post-turnover stabilization, early-life performance and defect resolution.
Plan with business partners when carrying out their requirements so that datacenter availability, safety and security are maintained.
4. Incident Management, Reliability and Risk
Serve as the senior IT escalation point for the metro. Take part in, and lead where appropriate, every Sev 1 and Sev 2 incident bridge affecting Microsoft cloud services in Charlotte, including communication with customers and senior leadership.
Approve root-cause analyses and postmortem reports, and drive improvement plans and corrective and preventive actions to completion.
Prevent IT infrastructure and operational risk before it affects safety, security, availability, capacity delivery, cost or schedule, or creates long-term technical debt.
Use incident trends, hardware failure data, commissioning findings and field experience to find systemic risks. Partner with engineering, OEMs and vendors to resolve them.
Make sure IT work in live environments goes through rigorous change management, including risk assessment, Method of Procedure (MOP) and Emergency Operating Procedure (EOP) review, and maintenance-window planning, to protect customer availability.
Own the metro IT risk register and make sure risks, dependencies and ownership gaps are tracked, escalated and closed.
5. Financial and Vendor Management
Own the metro IT Operations budget, including detailed budgets, forecasts, and management of operating and capital spend. Make tradeoff decisions that follow sound fiscal practices.
Lead budget planning and demand-cost forecasting. Make sure business leaders understand how service-management issues affect cost, risk and staffing, and negotiate for the resources the organization needs.
Manage and oversee IT vendor and partner contracts and relationships, including IT service providers, contracted labor, OEMs and partner support teams. For leased facilities, coordinate with landlords and their operators on IT-related requirements.
Hold vendors accountable for performance, quality and commercial results, and recommend extra funding or resources for pilots, task forces or growth where needed.
6. Governance, Metrics and Executive Communication
Establish consistent IT Operations governance across the metro, with clear decision rights, escalation paths, response expectations and accountability.
Set and monitor meaningful KPIs. Examples include SLA attainment, on-time capacity delivery, readiness milestone completion, incident and repair turnaround, issue aging, turnover defect trends, asset accuracy, safety performance and cost efficiency.
Give the Metro Director and regional leadership concise reports on IT portfolio health, readiness, schedule, financial performance, risk and key decisions.
Translate complex technical and operational issues into clear, decision-ready information for senior leadership.
Represent IT Operations in metro, regional and CO+I leadership forums, design reviews and readiness governance.
7. Cross-Functional Partnership and One Microsoft
Serve as the single point of IT Operations integration for the metro across CE, IAM/Logistics, DCD, DCE, Commissioning, Physical Security, Environment Health & Safety, network and hardware engineering, and global and regional teams.
Partner with the Metro Director and peer functional leaders to align metro priorities, coordinate cross-campus planning, manage dependencies and resolve ownership gaps.
Find opportunities to collaborate across groups, make sure cross-team commitments are set, and achieve scale by enabling the work of others.
Support global and regional initiatives such as environmental health and safety programs, risk assessments, audits, compliance and certifications.
Act as a trusted advisor to a wide network of colleagues and bring diverse viewpoints together to solve organization-wide problems.
8. Safety, Security, Culture and Ownership
Build a culture of safety, security, quality, compliance and customer obsession in every part of IT operations.
Follow the runbooks provided by the Environment, Health & Safety division, and report any safety or security issue or concern immediately.
Take pride and personal accountability for end-to-end service quality, completeness and the resulting customer experience. Find unaddressed issues and resolve them, escalate them, or find the right owner.

Learn, live and coach the One Microsoft culture and values. Lead through change by bringing clarity, generating energy and delivering success.

High School Qualification or equivalent AND 10+ years experience of mission-critical service management (e.g., providing IT services, manufacturing, warehouse, retail, military, or managing physical operations in an IT and/or critical environment infrastructure) OR equivalent experience
3+ years people management experience.

title: Director, Social & Creator Marketing - Minecraft
description:
Overview
At Mojang Studios, the creators of Minecraft, we are on a mission to build a better world through the power of play.
Why play? Well, play is at the heart of everything we do. It’s the blocky backbone of our games, the core of our development philosophy, and even the origin of our name. From the relentless experimentation of our endlessly inspiring community to the classrooms where Minecraft has become an essential teaching tool, play is the bedrock of our existence.
We enable millions to create and play together, connect people across the globe, and foster a community that is among the most active and passionate in the world. Our community is global and incredibly diverse. When we are developing anything within our franchise, we keep this in mind. We want everyone to not only feel included in Minecraft, but also to see themselves in what we make. Our goal is for the Mojang Studios team to be as diverse as our community.
Minecraft leads how Minecraft builds audiences, participates in culture, and deepens relationships with players, creators, and fans globally. The Director, Social & Creator Marketing is responsible for a connected global organization spanning organic social, including international and local market channels, influencer and community marketing, affiliate marketing and creator commerce, and editorial and direct-to-fan programming.
Exceptional cultural and creative judgment is essential. The leader must understand culture and community, recognize what is authentically Minecraft, and translate emerging audience and creator signals into distinctive ideas, stories, programming, and experiences that people want to watch, share, create with, and participate in.
The Director, Social & Creator Marketing works closely with Performance Marketing to connect these capabilities with paid media and player lifecycle marketing around shared audience, franchise, and business priorities. The leader builds the organization, talent, capabilities, partnerships, and ways of working needed to deliver impact on a global scale and compound that impact over time.
In the end, it’s the people of Mojang Studios that make this place truly special. When you join, you’ll find yourself in the company of incredibly bright, warm, and creative individuals – all united and working toward a single goal. Come help us reach it!

Define how Minecraft builds audiences, participates in culture, and deepens relationships with players, creators, and fans. Recognize what is authentically Minecraft and translate emerging cultural, audience, and creator signals into distinctive ideas, stories, programming, and experiences.
