Our approach is grounded in Cloud Solution Provider acceleration, co-sell precision, and performance accountability—executed consistently across all solution areas and every stage of the MCEM Win Formula. We are committed to delivering on our segment and revenue accountabilities by aligning execution with measurable impact, fostering partner transformation, and enabling scalable, outcome-driven growth.
The Global Partner Development Manager working with Telcos is a key role within Microsoft’s Channel Partner Sales organization. They are responsible for Microsoft’s business priorities through a set of high performing Telco partners, focusing on scaling sales and cloud adoption in the Small Medium Enterprise and Channel (SME&C) business via Telco Channels.
This role centers on strategic growth through Telcos through alignment of partner’s GTM strategy with Microsoft’s priorities and sales methodology. The GPDM is accountable for 360 degree partner performance and Cloud Solution Provider (CSP) revenue in SME&C.
As a Global Partner Development Manager (GPDM), you are accountable for the 360 degree partner performance and Cloud Solution Provider (CSP) revenue in SME&C. You will leverage your challenger mindset, deep technology and industry knowledge on Cybersecurity, Cloud & AI and Converged Communications along with the top class interpersonal abilities to empower our partners to bring market-defining solutions to our customers. This opportunity will allow you to accelerate your career growth as you work deeply with highly complex partner organizations, building solid relationships in the C-Suite and collaborating across multiple internal stakeholders to exceed budget targets, retain/secure partner commitment to Microsoft and drive profitable growth for both Microsoft and the partner.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.
Responsibilities
In this role, the Telco GPDM will own a broad set of responsibilities to drive partner performance and business outcomes.
Advanced understanding of the Telco Industry to align partners’ GTM with Microsoft’s business priorities.
Have an Intermediate/Advanced knowledge on Microsoft solutions with an ability to develop, use, and/or discuss Microsoft products and strategy (Microsoft Cloud & AI platform, Security and AI Business Solutions) with both the internal teams and customers/partners.  Guide business and technical decision makers on increasing compliance, reducing risk, and creating managed services practices, Security Operation Centers and GTM Offerings on top of the Microsoft Security platform.  Serve as the as the GTM Solution specialist in the Cyber security space for the regional and Global partner team. Work with other security organizations (Engineering, Marketing, Solution Specialists) in Microsoft to generate and reuse content to accelerate partner GTM offers and influence prioritization of solution development.
Develop Strategic Partner Plans: Create and execute an impactful Partner Business Plan for each assigned Telco, aligning the partner’s business goals with Microsoft’s mission, culture, and sales targets. This includes defining clear revenue and solution milestones and regularly updating plans to reflect evolving priorities and opportunities.
Drive Sales Execution & Pipeline: Lead the partner to execute across all priority solution areas (e.g. AI Copilot, Security, Modern Work). Own the sales pipeline with the partner – from demand generation to deal closure – and drive conversion of at least 40% of inbound leads to qualified pipeline through rigorous follow-up and co-selling support.
Manage  CSP Revenue: Oversee and grow the Cloud Solution Provider (CSP) business through the Telco. Track CSP sales performance, address gaps, and implement initiatives to accelerate cloud consumption.
Leverage Programs (SureStep, Incentives): Orchestrate the effective use of partner investments programs like SureStep to build partner capacity and capability. Ensure programs are well understood and executed by the partner organization to maximize ROI and partner profitability.
Rhythm of Business & Performance Management: Establish a solid Rhythm of Business (RoB) with the Telco across both executive and working levels, including monthly and quarterly business reviews. In these reviews you will analyze performance against targets (revenue, new customer adds, and other performance metrics ) and set action plans. Continuously track and forecast performance using Microsoft tools (e.g. CRM dashboards, MSX Insights), maintaining a predictable cadence and early identification of risks or opportunities.
Stakeholder Engagement & Alignment: Serve as the primary liaison between Microsoft and the Telcos’ leadership. Engage with the partner’s executives (and Microsoft’s global/area execs) to maintain strategic alignment. Facilitate connections between the Telco’s and Microsoft’s teams, ensuring that partner-led deals and campaigns are integrated with local sales motions. Create trust and credibility through regular executive touchpoints and by addressing escalations or blockers promptly.
Business Development & Strategy Landing: Lead business conversations with partners to land Microsoft’s sales strategies and new initiatives. Introduce and drive adoption of new Microsoft offerings by articulating value propositions and market advantages. Co-develop go-to-market strategies with the Telcos to target new customer acquisition, cloud migrations, and upsell opportunities across their sales channels and affiliates.
Partner Coaching and Enablement: Act as a coach and advisor to the Telco’s sales and technical teams. Increase their proficiency in selling Microsoft solutions – e.g., by highlighting cross-solution play opportunities and guiding them to position multi-cloud or multi-solution deals  to increase Microsoft’s share of wallet. Encourage a “learn-it-all” culture within the partner team by promoting continuous learning, certification attainment, and use of Microsoft skilling resources (labs, bootcamps, etc.).

Overview
As the Growth Channel Incubation & Product Strategy Director , you will identify, shape, and prove the next generation of growth capabilities across Microsoft product surfaces. You will work at the intersection of product strategy, engineering, marketing, customer experience, and business growth to determine where new product-led growth opportunities exist and what Microsoft must build to realize them.
This is a builder role, not a traditional campaign management role. You will develop growth hypotheses, translate customer and business opportunities into product and capability requirements, influence product roadmaps, and lead incubation from concept through evidence-based scale, iteration, or stop decisions. You will establish the initial strategy, partnerships, success measures, and operating model for new capabilities, then transition proven capabilities to the teams responsible for activation and scaled operations.
Responsibilities
•    Define the next growth opportunities: Identify product surfaces, customer moments, ecosystem signals, and emerging capabilities that could become new growth channels. Develop a clear point of view on where Microsoft should invest and why.
•    Create product-led growth strategy: Translate customer needs and growth opportunities into strategies, value propositions, product requirements, experience principles, and measurable growth hypotheses.
•    Influence product and engineering roadmaps: Build trusted partnerships with senior product, engineering, design, data, and marketing leaders. Represent growth requirements early in product planning and influence what is built, how it is instrumented, and how it can be activated.
•    Lead incubation from concept to proof: Design and lead pilots that test new channel mechanics, customer experiences, and product capabilities. Establish success criteria, learning agendas, dependencies, and decision points before work begins.
•    Drive evidence-based investment decisions: Synthesize customer, performance, technical, and business evidence to recommend whether capabilities should scale, iterate, or stop. Communicate recommendations clearly to executive stakeholders.
•    Build reusable capabilities, not one-off programs: Create repeatable frameworks, design patterns, playbooks, governance, and initial operating models that enable successful concepts to be used across products, audiences, and growth motions.
•    Establish capability handoffs: Define readiness criteria and partner with growth activation and channel operations leaders to transition proven capabilities into scaled execution with clear ownership, documentation, and measurement.
•    Shape the external and internal point of view: Develop a deep understanding of product-led growth practices inside and outside Microsoft. Apply relevant insights to Microsoft’s ecosystem and articulate a compelling vision for how growth capabilities should evolve.
•    Lead through influence: Drive clarity and momentum across complex, cross-organizational initiatives without relying on direct authority. Anticipate barriers, align stakeholders, make tradeoffs visible, and accelerate decisions.

The Azure Storage Platform team designs, builds and deploys the hardware and software foundation behind Azure Storage IaaS, spanning SSDs (Solid State Drives), HDDs (Hard Disk Drives) and Data Processing Units (DPUs). DPUs open new opportunities to improve performance, cost and efficiency by offloading storage, networking and security workloads from host CPUs (Central Processing Units).
We’re looking for a Principal Technical Program Manager to help bring these capabilities to Azure, leading delivery from platform development and storage software integration through validation and deployment across Azure regions. You’ll bring together engineering teams across Microsoft and external partners to evaluate technical options, align priorities and move complex programs forward. The work spans hardware, distributed storage and large-scale software delivery, with room to shape technical direction and guide decisions along the way. If you enjoy working across teams, bringing clarity to ambiguous problems and seeing plans become platforms running at Azure scale, this role offers the opportunity to help build the next generation of Azure Storage.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.

Lead DPU program delivery. Drive programs from requirements and hardware bring-up through pilot, general availability (GA) and fleet-wide deployment

Help teams resolve dependencies and adapt plans as requirements and technical findings evolve
Manage risks and escalations. Identify technical and schedule risks early, coordinate mitigations and bring clear options to decision-makers when trade-offs require resolution. Communicate with leadership. Provide concise updates on progress, risks, dependencies and decisions needed to keep delivery on track
Partner with technology providers. Represent Azure Storage in discussions with DPU silicon, SSD, HDD and server vendors on roadmaps, deliverables and issue resolution

title: Principal Value Creation Lead
location: United States, Multiple Locations, Multiple Locations
description:
Overview
The Frontier Transformation Framework helps our customers become Frontier Firms: organizations where AI is not a tool added to the business but part of the operating system the business runs on. The single biggest reason AI programs stall is not the technology; 95% of AI pilots fail to deliver meaningful P&L impact because they are deployed without a value hypothesis, measure the wrong things, or never baseline before building. Value Creation and Management is the discipline that closes that gap, turning AI from a cost center with unclear returns into a tracked investment with board-level visibility. The Frontier Transformation team is how the Microsoft Frontier Company, the organization this role sits within, delivers this: a small, human-agent team in which each member carries one of the Framework's eight capabilities into the customer, directs a set of digital co-workers to deliver at a scale headcount alone could not, and is designed to fade into a customer counterpart who can carry the work forward.
We are seeking a Principal Value Creation Lead  to define, design, and prove the business value of AI and agentic investment across strategic customer engagements. In this role, you will own the Value Realization Framework end to end: surfacing where AI investment aligns with a customer's strategic objectives, building the value hypotheses and investment cases that unlock funding, declaring the measurement approach before anything is built, and proving realized outcomes against baselines once solutions are live. You will operate at the intersection of finance, business strategy, engineering, and field delivery, working directly with CFOs, executive sponsors, account teams, Industry Business Architects, and delivery pods.
This is a role for people who are equally comfortable in a CFO-led value workshop and in the detail of a P&L model, who can move from strategic ambition to a defensible financial figure, and who are energized by making value real rather than anecdotal. You will help customers see, fund, and capture the value of becoming a Frontier Firm, while shaping the reusable value patterns, benchmarks, and playbooks that scale this discipline across industries. If you are excited by the opportunity to make AI investment measurable, fundable, and provable, this role is for you.
Responsibilities
Lead value discovery through the Value Realization Framework, running facilitated (often CFO-led) workshops that identify where AI and agent investment aligns with the customer's strategic business objectives.
Build and own value hypotheses for each candidate use case, framed as a single testable statement and mapped to the four value themes: Enrich Employee Experience, Reinvent Customer Experience, Reshape Business Processes, and Bend the Innovation Curve.
Produce value-ranked agent backlogs, prioritizing opportunities by business value, feasibility, and time-to-impact using the Value Rubric and Frontier Guide (Today-vs-Frontier benchmarks).
Develop the Business Case that unlocks funding: a three-scenario financial model (Conservative, Expected, Optimistic) with ROI, time-to-break-even, sensitivity analysis, and an explicit cost of inaction.
Design the Measurement Spine, decomposing the sponsor's Impact KPI into Value Driver KPIs, and defining Adoption Diagnostics (Reach and Depth) that explain why the numbers moved.
Capture before-and-after baselines for every use case ahead of deployment, using quantitative snapshots, user surveys, and stakeholder interviews, so impact can be proven afterward.
Build and run measurement instruments, including the Copilot Dashboard in Viva Insights and the per-engagement Pulse Dashboard (Power BI) that reads the Measurement Spine live.
Produce the Agentic Business Impact Report, correlating AI and agent deployment to financial KPIs such as cycle time, cost-to-serve reduction, and throughput improvements tied to specific workflows.
Own the P&L of every Frontier Loop, accounting for human labor, agents, tokens, licenses, and value leakage, and surfacing where projected value is or is not being realized.
Assess Scale Readiness at the end of each engagement (Scale / Sustain / Pivot) and translate the final value assessment into a defensible financial figure that informs the scale decision.
Develop reusable value patterns, rubrics, benchmarks, and playbooks that scale the Value Creation and Management discipline across industries and regions, and transfer the practice to the customer's own finance and value owners.
Success in this role looks like
Every AI and agent investment is anchored to a value hypothesis and a strategic KPI, with a clear baseline captured before anything is built.
Sponsors secure funding because the Business Case is credible, transparent, and directly tied to the customer's strategic priorities.
Customers move from concept to funded delivery to proven, board-visible P&L impact rather than anecdotal productivity gains.
Value is measured live against baselines, and the scale decision (Scale / Sustain / Pivot) is grounded in evidence.
The customer's own finance and value owners can run the Value Realization Framework after the engagement fades, and field learnings improve the value playbooks and benchmarks used everywhere else.
Qualifications
Required/minimum qualifications
Master's Degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or related field AND 6+ years experience in technology solutions, practice development, architecture, consulting, and/or technology domain (e.g., Security)
OR Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or related field AND 8+ years experience in technology solutions, practice development, architecture, consulting, and/or technology domain (e.g., Security)
OR equivalent experience.
2+ years managing multiple projects or portfolios.
1+ year(s) experience leading blended, multidisciplinary teams.
Additional or preferred qualifications
Demonstrated experience building business cases, ROI and financial models, and value hypotheses that have secured investment or funding decisions.
Experience defining KPIs and success metrics and measuring realized business outcomes against baselines.
Experience working directly with business and finance stakeholders (including CFO or executive sponsors) to scope ambiguous problems and quantify business value.
Analytical and quantitative skills, including financial modeling, scenario analysis, and sensitivity analysis.
Ability to translate complex technical and AI concepts into clear business value, financial terms, and executive-ready recommendations.
Proficiency with data analysis and reporting tools such as Excel and Power BI (or comparable BI/dashboarding platforms).
Demonstrated ability to operate across finance, strategy, engineering, product, and delivery teams.
Problem-solving skills in ambiguous, fast-moving environments.
Experience with value realization, value engineering, or business value frameworks in an enterprise consulting or technology environment.
Familiarity with AI, agentic AI, and Microsoft platforms such as Microsoft Copilot, Viva Insights (Copilot Dashboard), Azure AI Foundry, and Microsoft Fabric.
Experience designing measurement systems and building live dashboards (for example, Power BI) that track KPIs against baselines.
Understanding of digital-labor economics, including the cost structure of agents, tokens, and licenses, and how to account for value leakage.
Industry depth in one or more sectors such as financial services, life sciences, manufacturing, energy, retail, or the public sector.
Experience shaping SOWs, effort estimates, and success criteria, and defining value governance for large transformation programs.
Ability to work with executive sponsors, finance leaders, business owners, and delivery teams, and to transfer value practices to a customer's own people.

title: Regional Managing Director, Data Center Community, Pecos, TX
description:
Overview
The Regional Managing Director, Data Center Community is an externally facing leadership role responsible for earning and sustaining trust in a major Microsoft data center community or regional cluster of communities. The role serves as Microsoft’s local community leader, local stakeholder point of contact, and chief spokesperson for the assigned region, representing the company with civic leaders, elected officials, business organizations, education and workforce partners, nonprofits, media, and community stakeholders.
This position is designed for a high-visibility data center environment where local trust, transparent communications, public engagement, and community benefit are central to Microsoft’s long-term license to operate. The Managing Director leads a regional team that includes a Community Manager and a Communications Manager and works in close partnership with the local data center operations, as well as Microsoft legal, government affairs, philanthropic and communications teams to deliver a coordinated, locally empowered, and campaign-ready approach.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.
Role Scope and Leadership Model
Lead Microsoft’s regional data center community strategy, including local stakeholder engagement, public narrative, community investment,  and trust-building priorities.
Serve as the chief local spokesperson for the region, shaping Microsoft’s voice in community forums, public events, local media engagements, business and civic convenings, and high-stakes community conversations.
Manage and guide a regional team and budget consisting of a Community Manager and a Communications Manager, setting priorities, aligning execution, and ensuring the team operates as one integrated local function.
Partner closely with the local data center operations leader to align community engagement, communications, and operational priorities, ensuring Microsoft shows up as a coordinated and accountable neighbor.
Coordinate with regional and national surge teams when new market entry, permitting, zoning, local controversy, media attention, or urgent community concerns require additional support.
Manage a locally focused budget to enable local partnerships and support community priorities in relation to the data center and its operations.
Responsibilities
Regional Leadership and Community Strategy
Own and accountable for the integrated community engagement strategy for the assigned data center region, translating Microsoft’s public  Community-First AI Infrastructure commitments into locally relevant plans, partnerships, communications, and measurable outcomes.
Build and sustain trusted relationships with local elected officials, civic leaders, business organizations, education and workforce institutions, nonprofits, labor partners, community advocates, and other priority stakeholders.
Represent Microsoft as a trusted local leader in public forums, community meetings, advisory boards, chambers of commerce, business councils, nonprofit coalitions, and other high-impact venues.
Anticipate community risks and opportunities, maintain a clear stakeholder map, identify emerging sentiment, and escalate issues quickly with recommendations for action.
Ensure community engagement begins early, remains transparent, and continues through the full data center lifecycle, including planning, construction, operations, expansion, and moments of heightened scrutiny.
Chief Spokesperson and Public Narrative
Serve as Microsoft’s chief local spokesperson for the assigned data center community, delivering clear, credible, plain-language messages about Microsoft’s investments, operations, community commitments and impact, and long-term presence.
Guide the local narrative across community engagement, media, social sentiment, public meetings, and stakeholder communications, ensuring consistency with Microsoft’s regional and national messaging while remaining responsive to local needs.
Prepare for and lead public-facing engagements such as town halls, hearings, office hours, tours, groundbreaking events, listening sessions, briefings, and community benefit discussions.
Work with the Communications Manager to develop talking points, FAQs, briefings, local proof points, media materials, rapid-response guidance, and storytelling that demonstrates Microsoft’s accountability and community impact.
Act as the trusted local voice during sensitive moments, helping Microsoft respond with transparency, empathy, speed, and operational accuracy.
Communications and Community Engagement Oversight
Lead the regional team’s budget communications and community engagement operating rhythm, ensuring the Community Manager and Communications Manager have clear priorities, coordinated plans, and defined accountability.
Oversee local communications strategy, including proactive storytelling, local media engagement, social sentiment monitoring, stakeholder updates, community event messaging, and crisis-response readiness.
Guide community programming and philanthropic investments, ensuring local grants, sponsorships, employee engagement, AI skilling, workforce initiatives, nonprofit partnerships, and education programs align with community priorities and Microsoft commitments.
Connect communications, media, and community efforts so local programs generate credible proof points and community voices that strengthen trust and demonstrate tangible benefit.
Ensure the regional team maintains accurate data, metrics, outcomes, and qualitative feedback to support internal reporting, public transparency, and continuous improvement.
Cross-Functional Coordination and Escalation
Serve as the central coordinator for community-facing work across various cross-functional internal Microsoft teams

title: Security Researcher
description:
Overview
The MDASH team is advancing how organizations discover and resolve vulnerabilities in source code. MDASH uses a multi-agent, multi-model system to analyze code, validate whether potential vulnerabilities are real and reachable, and provide developers with concrete fixes and guidance for verifying that code is no longer vulnerable. We are seeking a Principal Security Researcher to build and improve the AI-powered, agentic system at the heart of MDASH vulnerability discovery, validation, and resolution. You will combine deep vulnerability research with AI experimentation: researching vulnerability classes and language ecosystems, identifying representative evaluation targets, building and reviewing ground truth, analyzing missed and incorrect findings, and developing improvements that measurably increase recall, precision, consistency, and fix quality. We are looking for a hands-on vulnerability researcher who can read unfamiliar code, trace attacker-controlled data to security-sensitive operations, develop and use fuzzers and other analysis tools, reproduce vulnerabilities, assess exploitability and reachability, and determine whether a proposed fix addresses the underlying weakness. You will carry research from hypothesis through implementation and measurement, directly building and evaluating improvements to MDASH's agents, tools, model configurations, and analysis methods while collaborating with engineering and applied science partners.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.
Responsibilities
Conduct hands-on vulnerability research across vulnerability classes, languages, frameworks, and codebase architectures to discover and validate vulnerabilities, assess reachability and exploitability, evaluate fixes for security correctness, and identify opportunities to expand MDASH coverage.
Translate research and evaluation insights into implemented improvements to MDASH agents, tools, model configurations, and analysis methods, and measure their impact.
Identify representative evaluation targets and author trusted ground truth spanning vulnerability evidence, attack paths, severity, validation, and remediation.
Drive MDASH's eval-driven development and hill-climbing loop by running evaluations, uncovering patterns in missed and incorrect results, and creating adversarial and regression cases that turn blind spots into measurable capability gains.
Build research prototypes, fuzzing harnesses, datasets, graders, and automation that accelerate capability improvement.
Provide technical leadership across the MDASH security research team by shaping research direction, leading complex investigations, mentoring other researchers, and raising the quality of vulnerability research and implementation.
Collaborate across research, engineering, applied science, and product teams to deliver improvements, communicate results, and influence technical direction.
Qualifications
Bachelor's, Master's, or Doctorate Degree in Computer Science, Computer Security, Computer Engineering, or a related field OR equivalent experience.
8+ years of experience in vulnerability research, application security, offensive security, secure software development, program analysis, or related security work.
Demonstrated hands-on experience discovering, reproducing, and validating software vulnerabilities; assessing reachability and exploitability; and evaluating remediation correctness.
Experience with fuzzing and at least one additional vulnerability research technique, such as manual code review, static analysis, dynamic analysis, debugging, reverse engineering, symbolic execution, taint analysis, or exploit development.
Proficiency developing security research tooling or automation in one or more programming languages.
Experience communicating complex technical findings through clear written reports, vulnerability analyses, or presentations.

Deep knowledge of multiple vulnerability classes and their exploitation patterns, including memory corruption, injection, authentication and authorization, cryptography, deserialization, path traversal, server-side request forgery, and business-logic flaws.

title: Senior Researcher - Efficient AI
description:
Overview
Generative AI is transforming how people create, collaborate, and communicate—redefining productivity across Microsoft 365 for customers worldwide. At Microsoft, we operate one of the largest collaboration and productivity platforms in the world, serving hundreds of millions of consumer and enterprise users. Delivering these AI experiences at scale requires solving some of the hardest efficiency challenges in modern AI systems.
We are an applied research team focused on advancing efficiency across the AI stack, spanning models, ML frameworks, cloud infrastructure, and hardware. We drive mid- and long-term product innovation through close collaboration with research and product teams across the company. We communicate our research both internally and externally through internal technical reports, academic conference publications, open-source releases, and patents. Beyond producing research, we take responsibility for driving ideas through prototyping, validation, and production, with a bias toward real-world impact.
The candidate will work across the full stack—from large-scale serving systems to hardware- and kernel-level optimizations—exploring algorithmic, systems, and hardware/software co-design techniques. Areas of focus include batching, routing, scheduling, caching, endpoint configuration, and GPU architecture–aware optimizations. This role emphasizes end-to-end ownership, with responsibility for identifying high-impact problems and driving research ideas through prototyping, validation, and deployment to deliver measurable customer impact.
For more see: https://aka.ms/efficient-ai
Responsibilities
Formulate, develop, and evaluate new algorithmic and system-level approaches for end-to-end AI serving, using analytical modeling and large-scale measurement to study token-level latency, tail latency (p95/p99), throughput-per-dollar, cold-start behavior, warm pool strategies, and capacity planning under multi-tenant SLOs and variable sequence lengths.
Design and experimentally evaluate endpoint configuration and execution policies, including batching, routing, and scheduling strategies, tensor and pipeline parallelism, quantization and precision profiles, speculative decoding, and chunked or streaming generation, and drive the most promising approaches through robust rollout and validation into production.
Perform hardware- and kernel-aware optimization by collaborating closely with model, kernel, compiler, and hardware teams to align serving algorithms with attention/KV innovations and accelerator capabilities.
Build and benchmark experimental prototypes and large-scale measurements to validate research ideas and drive them toward production readiness; produce clear technical documentation, design reviews, and operational playbooks.
Publish research results , file patents, and, where appropriate, contribute to open-source systems and serving frameworks

Demonstrated experience in designing and optimizing efficient inference systems, combining foundations in algorithmic optimization, parallel computing, and request orchestration under strict SLO constraints with deep knowledge of attention and KV‑cache optimizations, batching and scheduling strategies, and cost‑aware deployment.
3+ years of experience with machine learning frameworks (e.g., PyTorch, TensorFlow) and inference serving frameworks (e.g., vLLM, Triton Inference Server, TensorRT-LLM, ONNX Runtime, Ray Serve, DeepSpeed-MII).

title: Firmware Engineer, Robotics
description:
About the Team

We are building general-purpose robotics. In the short term, we are focused on robots to support skilled workers to build our future infrastructure. In the long term, we imagine everyone having a personal robot doing anything they need. Progress is rapid, and based on a foundation of co-design between robotics hardware and ML research.

About the Role

As a Firmware Engineer, you will define and drive the architecture of embedded systems for next-generation hardware products. You will own foundational firmware decisions across real-time execution, device bring-up, hardware interfaces, fault handling, safety mechanisms, and production readiness.

We’re looking for someone with deep experience building safety-critical or high-consequence systems, where failures can have meaningful consequences. You should be comfortable reasoning about risk, designing for diagnosability and graceful degradation, and creating engineering practices that raise the reliability bar for the entire team.

You should also be unusually good at moving fast. Sometimes the right answer is a carefully reviewed architecture that will endure for years; sometimes it is getting a rough-but-useful prototype working by the end of the afternoon so the team can learn something concrete tomorrow. We value engineers who know the difference, make that call well, and can operate credibly in both modes.

You will be both a technical leader and a hands-on builder: setting direction, reviewing critical designs, unblocking the hardest problems, and writing production firmware when it matters most.

Our embedded stack uses a lot of Rust. Extensive experience in the language is a big help!

In this role, you will:

 - Rapidly bring up new hardware and set execution pace for the team.

 - Lead firmware architecture for embedded systems spanning boot, RTOS/runtime behavior, peripheral control, power management, communications, and field diagnostics.

 - Define engineering standards for reliability, fault tolerance, observability, and maintainability across the firmware stack.

 - Design and review safety-critical mechanisms, including fault detection, recovery paths, watchdog strategies, redundancy where appropriate, and safe-state behavior.

 - Build quick, scrappy prototypes when speed of learning matters, then harden the right ideas into production-quality systems.

 - Partner closely with engineers in hardware, software, and AI research from early prototype through production.

 - Build rigorous bring-up, validation, and release processes for embedded platforms.

 - Establish testing strategies across unit, hardware-in-the-loop, integration, stress, and failure-injection testing.

 - Drive root-cause analysis for subtle hardware, firmware, and system interactions.

 - Make clear tradeoffs across performance, memory, power, schedule, and safety.

 - Mentor firmware engineers and help shape a culture of urgency, technical rigor, practical judgment, and high-quality execution.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have extensive experience developing firmware in an iterative environment.

 - Get a thrill from bringing up new hardware and taking end-to-end ownership over ensuring it works.

 - Have led architecture and delivery for complex embedded products that shipped to real users or operated in demanding production environments.

 - Are deeply fluent in low-level languages (we use Rust!) and comfortable working close to hardware under real-time constraints.

 - Understand embedded systems from first principles, including interrupts, scheduling, memory layout, buses, DMA, timing behavior, and failure modes.

 - Have strong instincts for defensive design, fault containment, validation depth, and post-deployment diagnosability.

 - Know when to build the durable system and when to produce the fastest credible artifact that unlocks the next decision.

 - Communicate clearly across disciplines and can turn ambiguity into sound technical direction.

 - Care about building systems that are not only fast and capable, but also trustworthy.

 - Make heavy use of Codex, Claude Code, or similar AI-assisted coding systems to accelerate implementation, prototyping, debugging, and iteration.

Nice to have:

 - Experience with Rust in embedded environments.

 - Experience with Embassy or other async embedded Rust frameworks.

 - Familiarity with mixed-language firmware architectures, including introducing Rust incrementally into existing C/C++ systems.

 - Experience with ARM Cortex-M or Cortex-R platforms, RTOSes, and low-power embedded designs.

 - Experience building firmware for sensor-rich, latency-sensitive, or tightly integrated electromechanical products.

title: Incident Commander, Detection & Response - US
description:
About the Team

Security is at the foundation of OpenAI’s mission to ensure that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity.

The Security team protects OpenAI’s technology, people, and products. We are technical in what we build but are operational in how we do our work, and are committed to supporting all products and research at OpenAI. Our Security team tenets include: prioritizing for impact, enabling researchers, preparing for future transformative technologies, and engaging a robust security culture.

About the Role

As an Incident Commander on Detection & Response, you’ll lead the response to complex security incidents affecting OpenAI’s intellectual property, customer data, and infrastructure. You’ll establish response priorities, coordinate technical work streams, drive containment and recovery decisions within agreed authority, and keep stakeholders informed as facts evolve. You’ll work with security and infrastructure teams across endpoints, identity, cloud, and compute environments, maintaining clear ownership and effective handoffs across time zones. Detection engineering knowledge is a supporting requirement: you’ll use telemetry and detection logic to assess evidence, identify visibility gaps, and guide improvements that make incident response more effective.

In this role, you will:

 - Run incident command from initial assessment through containment, recovery, and closure, establishing severity, scope, response objectives, and escalation needs.

 - Assign work stream owners and coordinate investigation, containment, and recovery in parallel. Maintain a decision log and distinguish confirmed facts from assumptions.

 - Drive timely containment and recovery decisions with the appropriate owners, weighing security risk, evidence preservation, and operational impact within agreed decision rights.

 - Communicate incident status, impact, uncertainty, actions underway, and the next update to technical and nontechnical stakeholders.

 - Manage cross-time-zone handoffs with explicit command ownership, current status, outstanding risks, pending decisions, and next actions.

 - Improve response readiness through exercises, playbooks, and post-incident reviews; track agreed corrective actions with their owners.

 - Partner with detection engineers to evaluate telemetry and detection quality, close incident-related visibility gaps, and prioritize practical response automation.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have personally led complex security incidents as incident commander or an equivalent response lead, with clear examples of decisions, delegation, escalation, and outcomes.

 - Make sound decisions with incomplete information and revise them as evidence changes, balancing containment urgency with operational impact.

 - Coordinate responders across teams and time zones, resolve conflicting priorities, and maintain clear ownership during handoffs.

 - Communicate calmly and precisely under pressure, including concise stakeholder updates and explicit statements of uncertainty.

 - Have the security and infrastructure fundamentals to challenge investigation findings and assess containment and recovery options.

 - Understand detection engineering, including telemetry coverage, detection logic, false positives and false negatives, and validation. Can query and interpret evidence to support response decisions.

 - Turn incident lessons into practical improvements to readiness, playbooks, detection coverage, and response tooling.

We’re building experiences within ChatGPT and integrations with tools such as CAD, eCAD, CAE, and simulation software to support engineers from early concepts through design, validation, and preparation for production.

We operate as a small founding team, working directly with customers and closely with research, product, data science, and forward-deployed engineering. We learn by building, putting products in users’ hands, and using their feedback to guide what comes next.

title: Security Incident Response Team Manager
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

Ensuring that advanced AI benefits humanity requires protecting the research, infrastructure, and trust that make its development and deployment possible. OpenAI Security defends our model IP, people, products, and users against sophisticated adversaries across GPU supercomputing, multicloud environments, datacenters, and emerging agent systems. The Security Incident Response Team (SIRT) leads the response when those defenses are tested—establishing what happened, limiting harm, and strengthening our ability to protect frontier AI.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for a hands-on technical leader to build the incident response team that protects OpenAI as AI capabilities and the threats surrounding them evolve. You will command consequential incidents, lead technically demanding investigations, and make containment and recovery decisions when evidence is incomplete and the stakes are high. You will also shape how frontier models change incident response: using OpenAI’s own technology to help responders connect evidence, test hypotheses, and act effectively at a scale that manual workflows cannot support. Partnering with Research, Infrastructure, Product Security, Enterprise Security, IT, and Engineering, you will build exceptional responders, dependable AI-powered capabilities, and stronger defenses through every investigation.




IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Hire, coach, and develop exceptional incident responders who combine investigative depth, engineering ability, and sound judgment. Build a team that challenges assumptions, surfaces uncertainty early, and uses AI to expand its capabilities. Develop technical leaders who can make and explain difficult decisions under pressure.

 - Lead incident command for complex threats to OpenAI’s research, products, and infrastructure. Establish severity and scope, coordinate investigation workstreams, and weigh containment options against ongoing exposure and disruption to research or production.

 - Build and ship agentic capabilities using OpenAI’s models for evidence collection, investigation context, response coordination, and bounded response workflows. Partner with platform engineers to integrate tools and data, evaluate accuracy and failure modes, and ensure reliable, auditable operation with human approval for consequential actions.

 - Set investigation standards for sophisticated adversaries and insider threats across identity, endpoints, cloud, Kubernetes, and large-scale compute. Help responders reconstruct activity, test competing hypotheses, preserve evidence, and make uncertainty explicit.

 - Drive incidents to verified closure. Work with accountable owners to validate containment and recovery, document remaining risk, and track corrective actions that reduce the likelihood or impact of recurrence.

 - Coordinate with engineering, infrastructure, legal, privacy, and other stakeholders throughout an incident. Give executives clear updates on impact, uncertainty, decisions, and the next update without overstating what the evidence supports.

 - Build sustainable on-call coverage, escalation paths, and handoffs across regions. Balance urgent response with training and planned improvements, and protect the team’s ability to recover after demanding incidents.

 - Build readiness into new research and infrastructure capabilities with their owners. Exercise playbooks, escalation paths, and containment options, including scenarios involving agents operating across systems at scale.

 - Turn incident evidence into stronger defenses with Detection Engineering, Threat Intelligence, Security Observability, and security platform teams. Identify what should have exposed an intrusion earlier, what prevented a faster or more confident investigation, and which capabilities would have changed the outcome. Translate those findings into tested improvements with clear owners.

 - Prioritize improvements using incident outcomes and readiness evidence. Measure response quality and effectiveness, make tradeoffs explicit, and address recurring friction without reducing success to ticket volume or speed alone.

 - You are motivated by the responsibility of protecting frontier AI. You want to understand how powerful new systems can fail or be compromised, help their builders move forward securely, and use the same advances in AI to strengthen defenders.

 - You are a hands-on builder with deep investigation expertise across identity, cloud, host, and infrastructure systems. You can prototype tools, write scripts or code, and coach responders through difficult evidence questions, including unfamiliar parts of the stack.

 - You have commanded consequential incidents involving capable adversaries, leading technical teams and senior stakeholders from uncertain signals through verified recovery. You make timely, defensible decisions with incomplete information, recognize when new evidence requires a change in direction, and remain accountable for the consequences.

title: Senior Manager, Accounts Payable - Payments
description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Procurement team makes working with the world easy, fast, and safe. We connect supplier readiness, purchasing, invoicing, and payment so teams can move with confidence as OpenAI scales. Accounts Payable provides the trusted data, dependable execution, and financial discipline behind that experience.



About the Role

We’re looking for an Accounts Payable Senior Manager to own and scale supplier payment operations. You’ll be responsible for accurate, timely payments, strong controls, and dependable service as OpenAI grows.

This is a hands-on leadership role. You’ll review and approve supplier payment runs, oversee work initiated by our BPO teams and AP agents, as well as personally resolve complex exceptions. You’ll stay close to execution during volume spikes and month-end close while building the processes, coverage, and systems the team needs to scale.

You’ll partner with Procurement, Supplier Master Data Operations, Accounting, Treasury, Tax, Finance Systems, and existing AP processing teams to make payments reliable from payment readiness through settlement reconciliation. You’ll clarify handoffs, address recurring failures, and improve ERP, banking, and procurement workflows. You’ll also apply automation and AI where they improve accuracy, service, or team capacity, with appropriate controls and human review.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office (Mon-Wed) per week and we offer relocation assistance to new employees.



We’re looking for someone with:

 - Strategic AP leadership and a hands-on approach to scaling systems and processes, with strong attention to detail.

 - Demonstrated ownership of complex indirect AP and supplier-payment operations, including PO and non-PO workflows.

 - Experience leading teams or outsourced delivery partners, setting expectations, developing capability, and managing performance.

 - Strong payment-control judgment and experience investigating duplicates, bank-detail changes, and payment failures.

 - Working depth in AP accounting, reconciliations, accrual inputs, and close coordination.

 - Experience translating AP needs into ERP or procurement-system improvements with measurable results.

 - Clear communication and the ability to influence partners and senior stakeholders in ambiguous situations.



In this role, you will:

 - Own supplier payment operations: Review and approve payment runs for supplier and payment data accuracy, required approvals, and exception resolution. Oversee manual disbursements and payment inquiries within established authority and segregation-of-duties requirements.

 - Resolve complex exceptions: Act as the primary escalation point for payment holds, rejected or returned payments, potential duplicates, and close blockers. Work with Treasury, banking partners, Accounting, and AP processing teams to establish the status, resolve the cause, and verify the outcome before retrying or closing an issue.

 - Strengthen payment readiness: Partner with Procurement and existing AP teams to resolve invoice, PO, approval, and supplier-data gaps that affect payment. Establish clear owners and follow through on recurring upstream issues.

 - Support forecasting and close: Provide reliable payment forecasts and cash-needs inputs to Treasury. Reconcile payment activity and exceptions, including payments after AP close, so Accounting has the evidence it needs for close and cutoff decisions.

 - Maintain effective controls: Uphold SOX-aligned approvals, independent supplier bank-detail verification, segregation of duties, and audit-ready documentation. Support internal and external audits and remediate control gaps with the relevant owners.

 - Improve systems and processes: Define payment workflow and reporting requirements with Finance Systems and other partners. Test ERP and bank integrations, including host-to-host workflows, and introduce automation or AI with validated outputs, exception handling, and clear accountability.

 - Lead BPO delivery and capacity: Set clear SLAs and KPIs, review quality and performance, coach service partners, and maintain documented procedures and backup coverage. Plan for volume spikes and close demands.

 - Report performance and risk: Own clear reporting on payment timeliness, exceptions, rejection and return trends, forecast accuracy, service quality, and control issues. Explain priorities and progress to stakeholders and leadership.



You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Bring 8+ years in AP, payments, or related finance operations, or equivalent experience, with personal ownership of complex supplier-payment operations and material exceptions.

 - Have worked across indirect supplier spend in a high-growth or scaling environment, balancing immediate delivery with durable process improvements.

title: Thermal Engineer
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops silicon and system-level solutions designed for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. The team is responsible for building the next generation of AI-native silicon while working closely with software and research partners to co-design hardware tightly integrated with AI models. In addition to delivering production-grade silicon for OpenAI’s supercomputing infrastructure, the team also creates custom design tools and methodologies that accelerate innovation and enable hardware optimized specifically for AI.


ABOUT THE ROLE

We are looking for an experienced Thermal Engineer with 7+ years of experience in thermal management of IT hardware from chip/package to system levels. You’ll work alongside experts in thermal, mechanical, electrical, software, and systems engineering to support the design, analysis, and validation of thermal solutions that ensure the reliability, efficiency, and longevity of mission-critical hardware. This position requires strong analytical skills, hands-on testing experience, and the ability to work in a fast-paced, cross-disciplinary environment.


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Design and optimize thermal solutions for data center hardware, including chips, power modules, and system-level cooling architectures

 - Evaluate thermal performance at the chip, package, and board levels, addressing challenges related to power density, heat dissipation, and thermal interface materials

 - Perform thermal modeling and simulation to predict temperature profiles and identify thermal bottlenecks

 - Collaborate with cross-functional teams to integrate thermal management strategies into hardware design, from concept to mass production

 - Support lab testing and validation, including the setup of thermal experiments, data acquisition, and troubleshooting of thermal performance issues

 - Design and select thermal components, such as cold plates, heat sinks, fans, vapor chambers, and thermal interface materials (TIMs)

 - Work with firmware and electrical engineers to define and implement thermal control algorithms for dynamic power and cooling management.

 - Conduct feasibility studies and trade-off analyses to evaluate cooling technologies and improve system thermal efficiency

 - Partner with suppliers and manufacturers to support the development of custom thermal components and ensure quality in production


QUALIFICATIONS

 - Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Thermal Engineering, or a related field (Master’s preferred).

 - 7+ years of industry experience in thermal design, simulation, and validation for IT hardware

 - Proficiency in thermal simulation software and CAD tools

 - Strong understanding of heat transfer principles, thermodynamics, and fluid mechanics, with an emphasis on electronics cooling

 - Hands-on experience with thermal testing equipment, including thermocouples, infrared cameras, wind tunnels, and P-Q characterization setups

 - Experience in chip/package-level thermal analysis, including die-level heat spreading, and package thermal modeling

 - Ability to analyze experimental data, identify root causes of thermal issues, and implement corrective actions

 - Strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to perform first-principles calculations to support design decisions.

 - Self-driven, detail-oriented, and able to work independently or collaboratively in cross-functional engineering environments


PREFERRED SKILLS

 - 10+ years of industry experience in thermal design, simulation, and validation for IT hardware

 - Extensive experience with data center hardware or high-performance computing systems at scale

 - Practical experience in developing advanced cooling technologies

 - Familiarity with thermal control algorithms and dynamic thermal management techniques

 - Understanding of reliability testing, failure analysis, and thermal stress testing for electronic components

 - Experience working with suppliers and manufacturing partners to support thermal solution development and production ramp-up

title: Threat Detection and Response Engineering Manager
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

OpenAI’s mission depends on developing and deploying powerful AI responsibly. Security makes that possible by protecting our research, people, products, and users while enabling progress. We defend sensitive research and other intellectual property, customer data, and the infrastructure behind frontier AI—from GPU supercomputing and multicloud environments to datacenters and emerging agent systems. Threat Detection Engineering builds and operates the detections and investigative workflows that turn adversary activity into effective response.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for a hands-on technical leader to guide the engineers who identify and investigate threats to OpenAI and build the capabilities to contain them. You’ll hire and develop engineers, set technical direction, and prioritize risks to OpenAI’s intellectual property, customer data, and critical infrastructure.

Your team will take an agent-first approach across the detection and response lifecycle, using OpenAI’s models to develop detections, triage signals, investigate suspicious activity, and support bounded response and continuous improvement. You’ll turn advances in model capability into dependable defenses, own their effectiveness, and work with security, research, and infrastructure partners to ensure findings lead to effective action. You’ll establish where agents can act independently and where human judgment and approval are essential.




IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Hire, coach, and develop engineers. Set clear expectations, provide regular feedback, grow technical leadership, and build a team that reviews work rigorously and learns from missed detections and noisy signals.

 - Set a threat-informed roadmap. Prioritize detection work based on how external and internal actors could target the systems where we train and evaluate frontier models, the production services that run inference and power our products worldwide, the datacenter hardware and networks that support both, and the devices, identities, and applications employees rely on. Balance investment in emerging threats with closing known coverage gaps and keeping existing detections effective.

 - Own detection and investigation as a complete workflow. Embed agent-driven triage and investigation in the detections your team operates. Surface findings when the evidence points to a likely threat that warrants action. When a finding warrants formal incident response, bring the evidence to the Security Incident Response Team (SIRT) and support the investigation SIRT leads.

 - Build response and containment capabilities tailored to our infrastructure. Work with infrastructure and system owners to develop and test the controls responders need to contain threats in their environments. Define when human approval is required and how to verify that containment worked.

 - Apply models across the detection engineering lifecycle. Use OpenAI’s models to help develop threat hypotheses, author and test detections, deploy and tune them, and incorporate investigation findings into better coverage. Evaluate the effectiveness of individual agents and the complete workflows they support.

 - Turn model advances into tested defenses. Prototype new approaches using OpenAI’s models, evaluate them against realistic adversary behavior and analyst baselines, and move successful experiments into production. Use operational evidence to identify model limitations and partner with Research and Engineering to address them.

 - Anticipate emerging threats. Translate adversary intelligence and incident findings into testable detection hypotheses. Work with researchers and infrastructure owners on risks specific to a frontier AI lab, such as increasingly capable agents operating across systems with access to sensitive research. Determine what evidence would reveal compromise and what response would be effective.

 - Establish the visibility needed to detect, investigate, and respond. Partner with Security Observability and infrastructure owners to define telemetry and forensic data requirements. Drive improvements where missing evidence, unreliable data, or limited controls prevent the team from identifying threats or taking effective action.

 - Engineer for measurable security outcomes. Use replay, adversarial validation, and regression testing to assess whether workflows find intended threats, distinguish benign activity, and reach defensible conclusions. Establish code review, documentation, staged rollout, monitoring, and rollback practices. Measure coverage, investigation accuracy, time to identify threats, and effectiveness of response.

 - Contribute during incidents. The Security Incident Response Team (SIRT) leads formal incident response. Your team contributes investigative expertise and uses incident findings to improve detections.
   
   


YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:

 - Think like an adversary and demand evidence as a defender. You question whether apparent coverage would survive a determined attacker, distinguish plausible explanations from supported conclusions, and stay accountable for threats that existing tools and playbooks miss.

 - Have managed security or software engineers and can demonstrate how you have hired, coached, developed technical judgment, and improved a team’s ability to deliver.

 - Are a hands-on builder who can prototype tools, write and review code, and guide engineers through complex detection, investigation, and response designs.

 - Bring strong AI fluency and have built systems that test how models or agents can improve cyber defense. You have evaluated real security workflows against meaningful baselines and can explain what improved, what failed, and what you changed. You understand model failure modes and design reliable workflows with bounded permissions and clear human decision points.

 - Have built or operated threat detections and led technical investigations. You understand adversary tradecraft and can assess evidence, scope, and uncertainty across complex environments.

 - Understand how identity, endpoint, cloud, Kubernetes, and infrastructure telemetry supports investigations. You can reason about response and containment in unfamiliar systems and work with their owners to build practical capabilities.

 - Have used testing and operational feedback to improve security outcomes. You can explain tradeoffs among coverage, accuracy, speed, and human workload, and choose measures that reflect whether threats are being found and addressed.

 - Can build a focused roadmap and strong cross-functional partnerships in a rapidly changing environment. You enable researchers and engineers to move quickly while following through on security requirements and dependable operations.

title: Director, Mechanical Sourcing
description:
Our mission at ŌURA is to empower every person to own their inner potential. Our award-winning products help our global community gain a deeper knowledge of their readiness, activity, and sleep quality by using their Oura Ring and its connected app. We've helped millions of people understand and improve their health by providing daily insights and practical steps to inspire healthy lifestyles.
Empowering the world starts with living our values and empowering our team. As a quickly growing company focused on helping people live healthier and happier lives, we ensure that our team members have what they need to do their best work — both in and out of the office.
At Oura, our mission is to empower people to live healthier, longer. With our award-winning Oura Ring and app, we help millions of people understand their sleep, activity, and readiness so they can live healthier, more balanced lives.
We are looking for a Director, Global Mechanical Sourcing to lead the strategy, execution, and development of Oura’s global mechanical sourcing organization. This leader will own mechanical sourcing across current and future hardware programs, with global responsibility spanning the established Finland and US teams and broader regional supplier partnerships.
This is an established function with strong leaders and processes already in place. The Director will align mechanical sourcing strategy across team based in the US, Finland, and Asia; connect priorities across the portfolio; improve decision-making; and be accountable for the function’s results as Oura grows - building on what is working while addressing the gaps that require a stronger global approach.
The Director will lead through existing leaders and teams, develop sourcing talent, strengthen the operating model, and raise the bar for analytical standards and commercial discipline. The role will work closely with Product, Industrial Design, Engineering, Manufacturing, Quality, Program Management, Finance, Legal, Logistics, and senior leadership.
This role is for a leader who can set direction, stay close enough to the details to know what is really happening, lean in to contribute directly as necessary, and make decisions when the information is incomplete. The work will require resilience with suppliers, direct communication, and good judgment. The right leader will manage effectively up and down, stay accountable for outcomes, and invest deeply in the growth of their direct reports. They will hold themselves and the team to a high standard of integrity, collaboration, and follow-through.
This is a hybrid role requiring someone to work 2-3 days a week out of our San Francisco office.
What You Will Do
Set the global mechanical sourcing strategy
Define and execute a multi-year global mechanical sourcing strategy aligned to Oura’s product roadmap, margin goals, quality standards, launch plans, resilience requirements, and manufacturing footprint.
Set supplier architecture across regions, technologies, and production stages, including preferred suppliers, second sources, geographic diversification, and capability-development priorities.
Create or iterate category strategies for key mechanical commodities such as CNC, injection molding, stamping, MIM, die casting, surface finishing, coatings, structural components, die cuts, softgoods, and related packaging categories where applicable.
Translate market conditions, technology developments, supplier capacity, geopolitical exposure, and cost drivers into clear recommendations for senior leadership.
Build a global mechanical sourcing roadmap that aligns priorities, supplier architecture, and tradeoffs across regions, building on existing strategies and processes while closing the observed gaps.
Lead and develop the global team
Lead the global mechanical sourcing organization through its existing leaders, aligning regional priorities and setting clear outcomes and decision rights across regions, commodities, programs, and supplier relationships.
Set a high bar for performance, decision quality, communication, and follow-through while creating an environment where people can do their best work.
Build and execute development plans for managers and individual contributors, including coaching, feedback, career paths, succession planning, and opportunities for expanded scope.
Assess organizational capability and capacity against Oura’s product roadmap; hire, structure, and develop the team as the business grows.
Set a common operating cadence with consistent mechanisms for strategy reviews, supplier performance, risk escalation, negotiation planning, and executive updates.
Build a strong working culture across geographies, challenge the status quo with respect, and help the team stay focused when the work gets difficult.
Bring analytical rigor to cost and value decisions
Establish a fact base for mechanical cost and value decisions, including should-cost models, supplier benchmarks, cost-driver analysis, total-cost-of-ownership analysis, and scenario planning.
Create visibility into mechanical cost trajectories across the product lifecycle and partner with Finance and Product Cost teams to connect sourcing actions to gross margin and business plans.
Use data to evaluate supplier proposals, manufacturing alternatives, volume assumptions, tooling and NRE, yield, labor, material, freight, payment terms, and other total-cost drivers.
Standardize scorecards and review mechanisms that make supplier performance, cost, quality, delivery, capacity, responsiveness, and risk visible to the right stakeholders.
Make sure recommendations are grounded in clear assumptions, evidence, and a realistic path to execution.
Build vendor strategy and supplier performance

location: Palo Alto, California, United States; San Francisco, California, United States
description:
ABOUT QUINCE
Quince is a destination for builders, creators, innovators, and operators who want to come together and challenge the status quo. Our mission is simple: make really high quality essentials for really low prices, fairly and sustainably. We deliver on that mission through a unique manufacturer-to-consumer (M2C) model eliminating the layers of traditional retail that add cost and result in consumers paying more than they need to. We find, build relationships with, and work directly with the manufacturing partners behind some of the world’s finest products. From there, our teams design smart, efficient operational processes  and build and deploy proprietary technology, AI, and analytics to help us scale fast.
What began with a small assortment of elevated basics has quickly grown into a cross-category brand spanning apparel, accessories, home goods, and more. Today, tens of millions of people across a growing number of countries come – and return – to Quince because they trust us to deliver.
OUR CULTURE
Quince is a culture built for builders by builders. Our way of working starts with a blank sheet of paper. We question conventional thinking, use technology and data to uncover new opportunities, and move quickly to turn ideas into reality. We aren’t interested in replicating how others do retail. We’re building a better way – at a speed and scale unlike anything that’s been done before.
We dream big and chase the hard problems others shy away from. Rejecting long-held assumptions is part of our company's DNA.  Where conventional wisdom says you have to choose – soft or durable, speed or rigor, quality or price – we ask why that trade-off has to exist in the first place.
Our pace is fast and the bar is high because our customers expect a lot from us and we refuse to let them down. We believe the best results come from challenging ourselves, learning from one another, and building on each other's strengths.
Here, responsibility is not determined by role, tenure, or seniority. Every team member - no matter their level - has the opportunity to drive our business and shape our trajectory.
If you’re someone who likes to imagine new possibilities and build better systems rather than plug-in to outdated ones, Quince is the place for you.
THE ROLE
Strategic Finance Manager
This role reports into the Head of Corporate Finance/FP&A and serves as a senior strategic finance partner to leadership across the business. The ideal candidate brings a strong foundation in investment banking and corporate finance, with experience supporting complex, high-growth businesses—ideally within eCommerce, consumer, or other fast-paced, technology-enabled environments. They demonstrate advanced analytical judgment and deep expertise in financial modeling, forecasting, and strategic analysis, along with fluency in Excel, financial planning systems, and data visualization tools.
This individual is expected to independently lead high-visibility financial initiatives, translate data into clear, actionable recommendations for senior leadership, and serve as a trusted thought partner to cross-functional stakeholders. Success in this role requires comfort operating in ambiguity, a proactive problem-solving mindset, and the ability to scale processes and insights alongside a rapidly growing business. This person is required to be in office 4 days a week in San Francisco, CA or Palo Alto, CA.
Responsibilities
Serve as a strategic finance partner to senior leadership, owning forecasting, long-range planning, and performance analysis across key areas of the business.
Build and maintain sophisticated financial models to support strategic decisions, including scenario planning, sensitivity analysis, and business case development.
Lead the annual operating plan and quarterly re-forecast processes, driving alignment on assumptions, targets, and resource allocation.
Partner cross-functionally with teams across the company to translate operational drivers into financial outcomes and identify opportunities to improve profitability and efficiency.
Develop and track key company KPIs and unit economics, connecting operational performance to broader financial outcomes such as contribution margin, cash flow, and enterprise value.
Prepare and evolve Weekly Business Review (WBR) and board-level materials, synthesizing complex analyses into clear, actionable narratives for executive leadership and investors.
Deliver high-impact ad hoc analyses on strategic initiatives, investments, pricing, and growth opportunities to inform decision-making.
Drive continuous improvement in financial processes, reporting infrastructure, and planning systems to scale with the business.
Qualifications
Requirements:
Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, Economics, or a related discipline.
4 - 8 years of progressive experience, ideally combining investment banking or corporate finance with FP&A, strategic finance, or a similar role supporting complex, operationally intensive businesses, preferably in retail, consumer, eCommerce, or supply chain driven environments.
Demonstrated ability to operate as a trusted strategic finance partner, influencing decisions through strong cross-functional collaboration with operational, commercial, and technical teams.
Deep expertise in financial modeling, scenario analysis, and business case development, with a track record of evaluating tradeoffs and informing high-impact decisions.
Strong understanding of unit economics and customer economics, including contribution margin drivers, cost structures, and the financial implications of operational and growth investments.
Advanced proficiency in Excel or Google Sheets, including complex models and sensitivity analyses, along with hands-on experience using financial planning and reporting systems (e.g., Adaptive, Anaplan, Hyperion, NetSuite, or similar tools).
Solid command of accounting and finance fundamentals, including GAAP, general ledger review, and financial controls, with the ability to partner effectively with Accounting teams.
Exceptional analytical skills, with the ability to synthesize large, complex data sets into clear insights that influence executive decision-making.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with experience presenting structured financial narratives and recommendations to senior leadership.
High attention to detail paired with the ability to manage competing priorities and ambiguity in a fast-paced, scaling environment.
A proactive, intellectually curious mindset, with the confidence to challenge assumptions, identify risks and opportunities, and propose thoughtful, data-backed solutions.
Preferred:
Master's Degree (MBA) or relevant certifications (e.g., CFA)
Investment banking and/or private equity experience
Finance experience in a retail, e-commerce, consumer goods, or supply chain–driven industry

Oversee the design, review, and procurement of fixtures required for test execution. Guide test-profile and instrumentation strategies, including the layout, installation, and calibration of strain gauges, accelerometers, and high-speed cameras. Ensure that standards are met when post-processing and interpreting time-series and frequency-domain data and extracting key structural metrics such as fatigue limits, damping ratios, stiffness, and plastic deformation.
