This goes for the emissions-free Electric Adventure Vehicles we build, and the curious, courageous souls we seek to attract. As a company, we constantly challenge what’s possible, never simply accepting what has always been done. We reframe old problems, seek new solutions and operate comfortably in areas that are unknown. Our backgrounds are diverse, but our team shares a love of the outdoors and a desire to protect it for future generations. Role Summary As a Senior Lead Exterior Designer, you will play a pivotal role in shaping the visual identity and proportion of future Rivian vehicle programs. Operating out of our Irvine Design Studio, you will lead the exterior design narrative from early blue-sky ideation through production execution. Reporting directly to the Senior Director of Exterior Design, you will collaborate closely with digital sculptors, clay modelers, aerodynamicists, packaging engineers, and studio leadership. You are both a visionary stylist with exceptional aesthetic taste and a seasoned design leader capable of mentoring designers, navigating engineering constraints, and championing design intent to final tooling. Responsibilities Creative Vision & Leadership: Lead exterior design themes for next-generation vehicle architectures, defining proportions, surfacing language, graphics, and lighting signatures aligned with Rivian’s brand ethos. Concept to Production Delivery: Drive projects through every phase of the vehicle development cycle—from 2D sketch ideation and 3D CAS modeling to 1:1 clay refinement and Class-A surfacing buy-off. Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner closely with Studio Engineering, Aerodynamics, Body-in-White (BIW), Thermal, and Engineering teams to develop innovative technical solutions without compromising aesthetic integrity. Mentorship & Culture: Provide day-to-day guidance, creative inspiration, and critique to junior and mid-level exterior designers, fostering a highly collaborative studio environment. Executive Presentation: Prepare and deliver compelling design presentations, physical model walk-arounds, and visual assets to the Senior Director of Exterior Design, Head of Design, and executive leadership. Studio Hands-On Direction: Work side-by-side with digital sculptors (Alias/SubD) and clay modelers on the studio floor, translating sketches into clean, sculptural, production-ready form. Qualifications Experience: 10+ years of production and concept automotive exterior design experience within an OEM studio or high-profile automotive design consultancy. Proven Track Record: At least one production vehicle exterior to your credit (from initial concept sketch through to production sign-off). Education: Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Transportation Design, Industrial Design, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience). Skills & Mastery: Exceptional 2D visualization skills (analog sketching, Photoshop, Procreate). Strong 3D spatial awareness with hands-on fluency or deep working knowledge of Alias, Blender, V-Red, or digital modeling workflows. Deep understanding of automotive package architecture, hard points, aerodynamics, pedestrian safety regulations, lighting, and manufacturing feasibility. Experience working directly with clay modeling teams to refine surfaces under studio lighting conditions. Experience in multiple A.I. software used in the design process, presentations, story telling, etc. Mindset: An adventurous, collaborative mindset and push-the-envelope of vehicle typologies. Role Summary Rivian is on a mission to build the future of sustainable mobility, and our commercial operations are where that mission meets our customers. Our Enterprise Digital team designs the tools behind sales, fulfillment and service: the systems our teams use every day to sell vehicles, deliver them and keep them on the road. Designing enterprise tools at Rivian isn’t about back-office forms. It’s about software that people across retail, delivery and service depend on to do their jobs well, where clarity and speed directly shape the customer experience. You’ll take complex business processes and turn them into simple, intuitive tools. We’re looking for someone who is a natural systems thinker and a strong communicator. Our team is defined by our ability to ask good questions, get comfortable with complicated business functions, reframe problems simply and bring others along. Responsibilities Problem Framing & Strategy: Work with product, engineering and leaders in sales, fulfillment and service to find the real bottlenecks, help shape roadmaps and write clear design briefs with measurable goals. Field Research: Spend time in retail spaces, delivery centers and service centers to see how work actually happens, talk with the people doing it, and understand the friction and edge cases they face. Systems Thinking: Map complex business processes, policies and data, and turn them into clear user flows, information architecture and interfaces that reduce effort and error. Prototyping & Validation: Turn ambiguity into something people can react to, from sketches and wireframes to interactive prototypes tested with real users. Design System Contribution: Use and pressure-test Rivian’s design system, and partner with the Design Systems team to extend it for enterprise needs. Cross-Functional Delivery: Work closely with engineers through each sprint, document your designs clearly, and take part in QA/UAT to make sure what ships matches the intent. Communication & Storytelling: Explain your work clearly to leadership, field teams and partners, connecting design decisions to business outcomes and the customer experience. AI-Enabled Design: Use AI tools across your process (research synthesis, exploration, prototyping, documentation), and help find where AI-powered features can make our tools smarter. Qualifications Application Requirement: Please include a link to your portfolio (with credentials). Applications without portfolios and log-in credentials will not be reviewed. 5+ years of experience in product, UX or service design, or in a related field where you solved complex problems for real users. Systems mindset: You enjoy learning how businesses work and are comfortable diving into unfamiliar operations, rules and data. Experience with enterprise software, B2B SaaS or internal operational tools is a huge plus. A portfolio that shows how you think: Case studies that walk through how you framed a messy problem, made sense of complexity and reached a clear solution. Reasoning and process matter as much as polish. Curiosity and humility: You ask questions before jumping to solutions and are eager to learn from the people who do the work. Collaboration: Experience working with cross-functional teams in an agile environment. Tools: Proficiency in Figma and modern prototyping tools, and fluency using AI in your design workflow. title: Senior Software Engineer, Autonomy Evaluation & Metrics Platform
description: About Rivian Rivian is on a mission to keep the world adventurous forever. This goes for the emissions-free Electric Adventure Vehicles we build, and the curious, courageous souls we seek to attract. As a company, we constantly challenge what’s possible, never simply accepting what has always been done. We reframe old problems, seek new solutions and operate comfortably in areas that are unknown. Our backgrounds are diverse, but our team shares a love of the outdoors and a desire to protect it for future generations. Role Summary Rivian’s Autonomy Eval Infrastructure team builds the software that helps engineers understand and improve the ML models behind our driving systems and gives release teams evidence they can trust. Within Autonomy’s AI Platform organization, we connect model development with evaluation workflows, metrics, triage and visualization across simulation and real-world vehicle data. As a senior metrics-platform engineer, you will design, build and operate a substantial part of the platform that makes autonomy evaluation consistent and reproducible. Working directly with Perception, Planning and Systems engineers, you will connect model experiments to reliable metrics and help turn insights about model behavior, failure modes and generalization into improvements in models and data. This is a hands-on software engineering role. You will own projects through design, implementation, rollout and operation, make practical system-design trade-offs, and mentor teammates. As an early member of a newly formed team, you will help establish the engineering practices and interfaces that make the platform useful across Autonomy. Responsibilities Own the design and delivery of a metrics-platform area, such as the metric registry, computation services or comparison and reporting APIs, in partnership with the team’s technical lead. Design versioned metric definitions and data models for inputs, aggregation, slicing and results. Preserve provenance linking official evaluation runs to code, model, dataset and scenario versions. Build distributed computation and storage paths with idempotent execution, incremental processing and controlled backfills. Make informed trade-offs across throughput, latency, cost and reproducibility. Build comparison tools that expose coverage, sample sizes, uncertainty and changes in evaluation inputs. Help users distinguish model regressions from data, simulator or infrastructure failures. Partner with model developers to design evaluation experiments, inspect predictions and analyze failure patterns. Use the findings to guide model and data improvements, and build reusable evaluation harnesses that shorten the iteration cycle. Integrate metrics and regression checks into replay and closed-loop evaluation workflows and CI. Partner with domain owners on metric semantics and thresholds, and with Systems on evidence for release decisions. Deliver self-service APIs and scorecards backed by consistent definitions and results. Migrate existing consumers incrementally while preserving reporting continuity and traceability. Own reliability and performance for your services through testing, observability, incident investigation and operational documentation; measure improvements in turnaround time, correctness and cost. Write and review production code, lead design reviews for your projects, mentor engineers, and collaborate across Palo Alto, London and Belgrade to deliver software that users adopt. Qualifications 5+ years of professional software engineering experience, or equivalent demonstrated experience and impact, including ownership of production backend or data-intensive systems. Hands-on experience building software for autonomy or robotics, with direct exposure to evaluation, simulation, perception, planning or validation workflows. Strong Python programming skills, with the ability to write, test, profile and debug maintainable production software. Practical SQL skills, with AI coding tools expected to support writing and refining queries; ability to validate query logic, results and performance. Demonstrated system-design ability across service APIs, data modeling, distributed processing and storage, including failure recovery, consistency and performance trade-offs. Experience taking a project from requirements and design through implementation, rollout and operation, coordinating dependencies and communicating trade-offs clearly. Practical understanding of model inference and evaluation, including held-out datasets, generalization, reproducibility and model versioning, and the differences between open-loop replay, closed-loop simulation and real-world measurements. Ability to reason about sampling, confidence intervals, noisy metrics and valid comparisons, and to work with domain experts when stronger statistical analysis is needed. Experience with cloud infrastructure, containers, CI/CD and production observability, plus a track record of constructive code review and mentoring. Bonus Points Experience building metric registries, evaluation services, experiment-tracking systems or automated regression gates used by multiple engineering teams. Experience with Spark, Databricks, Delta Lake or comparable distributed data systems, and with AWS, Docker or GitLab CI. Experience migrating analytical or reporting systems without breaking downstream consumers, or linking metrics to scenario-level debugging and triage. Experience with PyTorch or similar ML frameworks, evaluation of end-to-end driving models, or connecting offline model metrics to closed-loop and real-world driving behavior. Role Summary This position is for a Service Advisor, the central point of contact and trusted guide for our owners throughout their service experience. This role requires a deeply empathetic, organized, and brand-focused individual who thrives on creating positive interactions and seamless processes. The Service Advisor is a critical liaison, translating complex vehicle needs into clear, confidence-inspiring communication for our customers, while coordinating flawlessly with the service production team. This job description outlines the full spectrum of skills required, and candidates will be assessed against this spectrum to determine the appropriate level for their expertise, from entry-level to senior advisor. This is a level-agnostic posting designed to recruit Service Advisor candidates across various seniority levels in the organization; specific level availability fluctuates and is determined by current business needs. The shift for this position is Monday through Friday (with rotational Saturday's) The Shift will be either 11AM-8PM OR 5PM-2AM This position comes with a 15% pay differential that occurs between 6pm - 6am Responsibilities Serve as the primary point of contact for owners, managing the service experience from initial appointment scheduling to vehicle handover. Listen actively to understand owner concerns, accurately document them in the repair order, and set clear expectations for the visit. Translate technical information from technicians into simple, understandable language for owners. Proactively communicate updates on vehicle status, managing timelines and ensuring a transparent process. Coordinate with the Parts and Production teams to ensure all aspects of the service visit are aligned. Prepare and explain estimates and invoices with clarity and accuracy. Ensure every owner leaves feeling cared for, confident in the work performed, and more connected to the Rivian brand. Manage internal systems to maintain impeccable records of all customer communications and repairs, ensuring all performance metrics are met or exceeded. Uphold Rivian's standards for hospitality, presentation, and process in every interaction. Act as the on-site liaison between Rivian’s centralized Service Support Operations Center and local Service Center operations. Support the launch and setup of new Service Center locations, training initiatives, and process improvements. Assist in warranty repairs and ensure compliance with state and federal automotive repair laws. Manage relationships with third-party vendors, documenting work orders and coordinating with production team to ensure seamless after-hours service completion. This role may require regular interaction with customers and their families, 3rd party affiliates, and suppliers within Rivian facilities, on mobile service routes, or at community outreach events. Must be available for a 40-hour work week, which may include weekends, holidays, and varied shifts based on business needs. Proficient with laptops, computers, and modern software suites (Windows, Google Workspace, Mac, CRM systems, etc.). Exceptional organizational skills, a meticulous attention to detail, and a passion for creating order. Outstanding written and verbal communication skills in English. Ability to perform physical tasks such as lifting up to 50 lbs., sitting, standing, walking, and frequent use of hands for grasping tools and data entry. Physical exertion may be required to perform occupational tasks (sitting, standing, walking, bending, kneeling, carrying, reaching, pushing, pulling, and lifting up to 50 lbs.). Ability to read and speak fluent English. Ability to see, read and interpret documents such as governmental regulations, safety rules, operating and maintenance instructions or schematics. Experience: Experience in a customer-facing role is required. Backgrounds in hospitality, retail, or fast-paced, system-driven restaurants are highly valued. Automotive service experience is a plus but not a prerequisite for entry-level roles. Proven ability to de-escalate sensitive situations and resolve customer concerns with empathy and professionalism. Experience managing complex scheduling, billing, and work order systems is a plus. Spectrum of Advisor Skills Customer Engagement & Hospitality: An advisor must be the face of Rivian service. Foundational skills include a warm, professional demeanor and the ability to follow established communication guidelines. An advanced advisor moves beyond guidelines to provide anticipatory service, remembering owner preferences, proactively addressing unstated needs, and building genuine, long-term relationships that foster trust and brand loyalty. Technical Acumen & Translation: A core competency is the ability to bridge the communication gap between the technician and the owner. A developing advisor can accurately transcribe customer concerns and look up vehicle information. A highly skilled advisor comprehends complex diagnostic concepts, asks clarifying questions of technicians, and can then translate that information into simple, clear, and confident explanations for the owner, ensuring they feel informed and empowered, never confused or intimidated. Process & Systems Management: The service experience relies on operational precision. An entry-level advisor manages the entire service workflow, from booking appointments to closing out work orders. description:
Who we are
Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.
About the role:
Samsara is looking for an experienced manager to lead SOX business process compliance and help keep the trust in our financial reporting as strong as the business we’re building. As part of our SOX Compliance team, you’ll help oversee and strengthen Samsara’s global control environment, protecting the accuracy of our financial reporting and keeping us compliant as we scale. You’ll partner closely with IT and business process owners to design and implement controls, spot gaps early, and drive remediation to the finish line. We’re looking for someone who takes real ownership. You bring deep, hands-on SOX expertise, a track record of delivering projects reliably, and the confidence to run with complex work independently. If you take pride in being the person others count on to get it done right, we’d love to meet you.
This is a remote position open to candidates based in the US  except the San Francisco Bay Metro Area, NYC Metro Area, and Washington, D.C. Metro Area.
You should apply if:
You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact – helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, reduce emissions, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.
You are the architect of your own career: If you put in the work, this role won’t be your last at Samsara. We set up our employees for success and have built a culture that encourages rapid career development, countless opportunities to experiment and master your craft in a hyper growth environment.
You’re energized by our opportunity: The vision we have to digitize large sectors of the global economy requires your full focus and best efforts to bring forth creative, ambitious ideas for our customers.
You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together and support each other. You will be surrounded by a high-calibre team that will encourage you to do your best.
In this role, you will:
Develop, lead, and execute periodic financial risk assessments, materiality calculations, and scoping of the SOX program
Develop and deliver training to SOX control owners, including process documentation, testing methodology, management review controls, and controls over Information Produced by the Entity (IPE).
Conduct walkthroughs across all business process areas and work with business process owners to ensure timely review and updates to the control documentation
Collaborate cross functionally to design leading edge practices with a financial compliance mindset across several complex business process areas.
Monitor and assess emerging financial reporting risks with the growth and evolution of the business and develop plans to implement appropriate controls to timely address these emerging risks
Ownership of control deficiency evaluation, aggregation analysis as well as development and execution of related remediation plans.
Help drive the SOX AI transformation strategy by identifying high-value opportunities, implementing AI-enabled solutions, and driving adoption and new ways of working across the global SOX organization.
Provide reporting to business leaders on program status, health, and effectiveness of the business process control environment
Collaborate and align with the company’s external audit and internal audit around financial reporting risks, design of ICFR monitoring systems,and SOX program approach
Champion, role model, and embed Samsara’s cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices
Minimum requirements for the role:
7+ years of SOX 404 / ICFR experience at a Big Four (internal or external audit) or combination of Big Four and public company experience
Hands-on experience with risk assessment, scoping, walkthroughs, control design, and deficiency evaluation
Strong knowledge of order to cash, procure to pay, financial close and reporting controls
Ability to identify, assess  and explain risks and control gaps clearly to executives and other non-technical audiences
Working knowledge of COSO 2013, PCAOB AS 2201, and SEC ICFR guidance, including management review controls and IPE
Bachelor's in accounting or finance (CPA and/or CIA preferred)
An ideal candidate also has:
Experience with financial systems such as Netsuite, Salesforce, Workday and Xactly
Experience using automation or AI tools to make compliance work faster, more reliable, and SOX compliant
Experience working closely with Internal Audit and External Auditors
Strong communication skills, including presenting to and influencing senior business leaders
Demonstrated success managing worksteams/project independently

description:

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.
Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. Recovering entrepreneur? Frustrated with bureaucracy? Want to build the team and write the roadmap, not inherit one?
We’re hiring Engineering Managers across multiple verticals. The nice thing about growing 30%+ at ~$2.1B ARR is that we need great engineering leaders everywhere, and we have the room to shape the team around the right person. You lead like a founder. We give you the platform to do it at scale.
About the role:
Samsara (NYSE: IOT) sits at the center of hardware, software, AI, and the physical world. The platform processes 25+ trillion data points annually from IoT sensors, cameras, and connected devices across thousands of organizations, and that dataset is compounding: it grew from 4 trillion to 25+ trillion in four years. We’re still early in turning that data into the products that will define how physical operations run, and we’re hiring the leaders who will build the teams that build what comes next.
We’re at ~$2.1B ARR growing 30%+ year over year, with 96% of our largest customers on two or more products. The fastest-growing divisions at Samsara are tackling the hardest, most ambiguous problems at the company: building new products from scratch, applying AI and ML to massive real-world datasets, and shipping capabilities that change how organizations maintain equipment, manage fleets, and run day-to-day operations. Most of this work is zero-to-one, at billion-dollar scale.
We’re looking for Engineering Managers who want to define what ships next by building and leading great teams. You’ll manage engineers across platform and product, and we’re open to shaping team scope around the right person’s strengths and interests. That window won’t stay open long.
This role is remote and open to candidates residing in the US or Canada. Relocation assistance will not be provided for this role.
You should apply if:
You want to impact the industries that run our world. The software your team builds will have real-world stakes: helping keep the lights on, getting food into grocery stores, keeping workers safe. What ships here isn’t metrics on a dashboard. It shows up on the loading dock, the job site, and the dispatch floor.
You want to build, not maintain. Samsara is in full growth mode. Your team will build new systems from scratch, not babysit old ones. You’d own entire problem spaces end to end, with the autonomy to set direction from day one.
You want to work where AI meets the physical world. Samsara has spent a decade building the largest proprietary dataset for physical operations. More connected assets generate more data, more data trains better models, better models drive more value, and more value wins more assets. The market and the opportunity here are what set us apart, not just the models.
You believe customers are more than a number. Samsara engineers have a rare closeness to end users. You and your team will participate in customer interviews, collaborate with product managers and customer success, and use that context to build products that solve real problems operators face every day.
You believe great teams are the real product. You get energy from hiring exceptional people, growing them, and creating the conditions for them to do the best work of their careers. The rate-limiting step on our teams isn’t tooling or process. It’s ambition, and your job is to unlock it.

Lead and grow a team of engineers: hire top talent, coach and develop individuals, manage performance, and build a culture of ownership, quality, and velocity.
Take ownership of technically complex, mission-critical areas and run with them. We want to point you in a direction and show up to the demo meeting impressed, not spend our weeks managing the details.
Define and drive technical strategy and roadmap for new products and platform capabilities, from backend services and APIs to the customer-facing UI.
Guide your team to design and ship full-stack features end to end, delivering AI-powered products that solve real operational problems across backend, frontend, and potentially mobile.
Partner with product, design, and customer-facing teams to translate ambiguous, real-world problems into clear technical plans, staffing, and measurable outcomes.
Oversee the systems behind AI-driven products, including data ingestion, APIs, and the workflows that put intelligence into the hands of operators, and stay close enough to the technical work to guide architecture and make sound tradeoffs.
Raise the bar across engineering through design reviews, hiring standards, mentorship of senior engineers and future leaders, and by setting the standard for quality, velocity, and craft.
Champion, role model, and embed Samsara’s cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices.
Minimum requirements for the role:
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or equivalent practical experience.
8+ years of experience in software design and development, including building and operating production systems at scale.
3+ years of experience directly managing software engineers, including hiring, performance management, and career development.
Strong technical fundamentals across backend services, APIs, and frontend (web or mobile), enough to guide architecture, review designs, and earn your team’s respect.
Familiarity with modern languages and frameworks (Go, Python, TypeScript/JavaScript, React, or similar).
Demonstrated experience leading cross-team or cross-org projects from inception through rollout, including managing ambiguity, driving alignment, and delivering measurable impact.
Experience building or leading teams that build AI-powered or data-driven products. You don’t need to train models, but you know how to take AI capabilities and turn them into products customers love.
Strong communication skills and the ability to translate between technical and non-technical stakeholders, including executives.
A track record of building: zero-to-one products, teams and systems you left in a meaningfully better place, or hard problems you refused to let stay unsolved.
An ideal candidate also has:
Experience shipping AI-powered features in production, whether that’s LLM-based products, agentic workflows, recommendation systems, or other customer-facing AI.
Experience leading teams through AI-augmented development workflows (Cursor, LLMs, etc.) to multiply output and accelerate delivery.
Background working with real-world operational data (telematics, sensor data, work orders, inspections) or a strong interest in learning the domain.
A proven track record of managing and developing senior engineers, building managers-of-managers, and influencing engineering culture, standards, and best practices beyond a single team.
Experience scaling teams through fast growth, including building hiring pipelines and onboarding.

title: Assembly Technician
description:
About Standard Bots

Standard Bots is America's largest manufacturer of AI-native industrial robots. Full-stack robots—hardware, software, and AI—all designed and assembled in Glen Cove, New York. The company makes AI-native robots anyone can buy and deploy, with customers ranging from family-owned machine shops to the Fortune 500. Customers include Sunoco, Lockheed Martin, NASA, and the U.S. Army, along with hundreds of manufacturers nationwide. Standard Bots raised a $200 million Series C at a $1 billion valuation from RoboStrategy, General Catalyst, Amazon Industrial Innovation Fund, and Samsung Next.


About the role

You'll build the robots that are showing up on factory floors across the country. Standard Bots is moving fast from prototype to high-volume production, and the people on the assembly line are the most important people in the building — this role sits right at the center of that. You'll work alongside the Production Supervisor and the engineering team, turning parts into precision robotic systems that are ready to work.

📍 Location

This is a full-time, on-site role at our Glen Cove, NY manufacturing facility, working first shift, Monday through Friday. We're unable to sponsor visas for this role.


What you'll do

- Assemble production robots and components to spec, following work instructions — hands-on work that takes a pile of parts and turns it into a finished machine.

- Run quality checks throughout the build, not just at the end, and report issues to the Production Supervisor as soon as you spot them.

- Keep your workspace safe and organized, in line with company and industry standards.

- Handle material movement and distribution to workstations so the line keeps running.

- Contribute to continuous improvement on the production floor — if you see a better way to build, we want to hear it.


What you'll bring

- A high school diploma or equivalent.

- 2+ years in a mass production or manufacturing environment.

- 1+ year of hands-on assembly, maintenance/repair, or tool experience.

- The ability to lift up to 50 lbs.

- Sharp attention to detail — you catch things, and you don't let things slide.

- Clear communication: you flag issues quickly and work well within a team.

- The ability to prioritize and stay focused when things are moving fast.

- A habit of showing up every shift ready to execute, and pride in clean, accurate assembly work.


Nice to have

- An Associate's or Bachelor's degree.

- Experience in automotive, aerospace, industrial, or electromechanical manufacturing.

- Machine shop or CNC equipment experience.

- Familiarity with OSHA standards and workplace safety practices.


Compensation and Benefits

The salary range for this role is $30.00 to $36.00 per hour, depending on experience. We are open to a variety of seniority levels for this role and will build compensation packages that are commensurate with seniority and skill level. Base salary is just one part of the overall compensation at Standard Bots. All Full-Time Employees are eligible for Employee Stock Options. We also offer a package of benefits including paid time off, medical/dental/vision insurance, life insurance, disability insurance, and 401(k) to regular full-time employees.

Typical activities include leading requirements analysis, solution design, technical development, and process improvement coupled with the ability to drive efforts and solution improvements effectively across various IT and business functions. In addition to delivering new technology and enhancing/supporting existing systems, an effective application developer lead contributes technical, expertise, negotiates platform priorities and drives alignment. As a application developer lead , you will lead...
Technical Design and Implementation Effectively leads and collaborates in planning, decomposing, estimating, scheduling, prioritization and resource allocation exercises. Takes the lead on prototype efforts for complex problems. Builds incrementally, with an eye toward vision of the final product. Provides transparency in approach and progress, throughout the process.
Leads the Development Team through the solution design process. Participates in requirements gathering and backlog refinement, takes the lead in shaping and guiding systems approach, drives project initiation, contributes to functional design, and leads technical design and development.
Develops software solutions to business problems. Leverages established design patterns and coding standards. Ensures solutions are secure, durable, scalable, flexible, and accessible and proactively mitigates against production support issues.
Automates test coverage per platform capabilities and requirements. Establishes and maintains continuous build and integration testing on applicable platforms and assists with manual system and integration testing efforts.
Contributes to and drives deployment approach, including planning and execution, data conversion approach, script development and execution, warranty period and transition of the solution to the platform's operational context.
Operates in both waterfall and Agile Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC) processes and methodologie

Identifies, influences, sells and prioritizes innovative platform opportunities, as well as technical debt, with regular reviews, creating programs and solutions to raise the level of the platform offering or remediate systemic operational problems.
Leads partnership efforts with cross functional teams, such as Infrastructure, Security, Architecture, QA and key Development teams, to strengthen and elevate the platform from a technology perspective. Successfully sees designs and solutions through enterprise processes and governance to ensure compliant, secure and supportable solutions.
Deepens vendor relationships to understand and influence vendor product offerings and roadmaps, improve support engagement and gain insight into technology trends.
Contributes to the platform development community by providing input, content and feedback on design patterns, coding standards, and shared libraries.

Supervises delivery of other developers on the team by setting priority and guiding deliverables.
Keeps projects on course by coordinating activities, monitoring project schedules and costs.
Effectively and efficiently analyzes options in a team setting to make sound decisions. Partners with vendors to improve delivery model and ensure success.
Represents the Development Team when engaged with cross functional teams, including functional analysts, Project Management, Development, Architecture, Infrastructure and the business customer. Negotiates, facilitates, and influences others to gain alignment and mutually agreeable outcomes in complex and ambiguous situations. Socializes technical approach and design to project team and corresponding dependent teams.
Takes on leadership opportunities within the development team. Initiates and facilitates team meetings to socialize technical ideas, encourages a culture of technical excellence among peers, and identifies good opportunities for adopting innovation.
Coaches and mentors other application developers learning new skills and technologies.
Exhibits leadership courage with respectful, articulate positions to influence critical technology solutions.

Tracks and communicates planned and in-flight business capability efforts, leads and influences approach, scoping exercises and resource estimation.
For a medium to large area of the business capability portfolio, responsible for rationalizing, designing and overseeing solution changes in the sustainment process.
Production Support for application and platform components Fulfills responsibilities for on call support, including potential coverage of pager rotation.
Leads and trains partners in collaboratively and effectively diagnosing, troubleshooting and remediating incidents and problems to support the end user community.
Initiates and leads root cause analysis efforts to identify and implement solutions to operational issues.
Creates and maintains operational Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) on items such as performance, service incidents and tickets set forth by the organization leadership. Identifies systemic problems that need holistic solutions and feedback into platform roadmap exercises.
Ensures documentation supporting training, system administration, deployment, and operational processes and procedures are created and well maintained.

8-10 years of professional industry experience with software development in Oracle OTM, Oracle ERP Supply Chain space.
2 years of leading teams of four or more software developers
Bachelor’s degree in computer science or related field

Technical Proficiency
Knowledge of data structures, algorithms and computer science concepts relative to the platform.
Mastery of relevant development languages, tools, frameworks, utilities and technical dependencies.
Understanding of implications from design and implementation choices toward building secure, scalable, durable, flexible, accessible solutions.
Ability to write and value high quality, reusable software with minimal defects.
Aptitude to pick up new technologies and trends, as they become relevant for the business and our platforms. Examples include IoT, Big Data, REST Services, mobile, and incorporating cloud components.
Thorough understanding of data transport mechanisms and integrations including synchronous, asynchronous, bulk data, tightly and loosely coupled methods
Ability to learn and incorporate new technologies, concepts and development languages.
Thorough understanding of application architecture, infrastructure and security concepts and technical implementation.
Ability to analyze, diagnose and propose solutions to user problems.
Ability to understand and escalate technical challenges with options and recommendations
Strong technical proficiency with Oracle Transportation Management (OTM) and Global Trade Management (GTM) SaaS, including application configuration, automation agents, data models, APIs and integrations, reporting, and troubleshooting.
Experience with Oracle Analytics Cloud (OAC), including Oracle Analytics Publisher reporting capabilities, for report development and support within the OTM/GTM environment.
Experience diagnosing and resolving complex technical issues across OTM/GTM, integrations, Oracle-based application and data processing, APIs, and reporting, including analysis of cross-system dependencies and failures.

This leader is the single point of reference for the hardware and software solution that powers roughly 5,000 licensed stores: Point of Sale, Point of Sale peripherals, order fulfillment, edge compute, endpoint management, and the API-driven integrations that connect Starbucks to each licensee's bespoke loyalty and sales systems. description:
UL Solutions is seeking a Global Market Access Solutions Manager with strong technical depth in global market access, product compliance, conformity assessment, and regulatory data. The role provides the solution expertise behind UL Solutions’ digital offerings, including AI-enabled services, Global Compliance Management (GCM), and builds partnerships with industry associations, standards bodies, and technical committees that influence how compliance requirements are defined and met.
The successful candidate can read a technical or regulatory requirement, explain what it means for a customer’s product portfolio and target markets and translate it into a clear solution design.  The role works with engineering, regulatory, product, and data teams to scope digital solutions accurately, leads activation and adoption for priority customers, educates sellers and customers, and represents.
UL Solutions in association working groups, technical forums, and standards development activity. The role helps make UL Solutions’ digital offerings credible, usable, and adopted through solution definition, activation, adoption, and customer education, and it strengthens that credibility through association and standards partnerships. Final technical authority remains with the appropriate engineering and regulatory experts.
This is a full-time, hybrid (3 days on-site) role and can be located and any of our US UL Solutions offices.
Solution Definition and Technical Discovery
• Lead technical discovery to define product scope, applicable standards, target markets, and regulatory requirements and identify where UL Solutions can create value.
• Translate complex technical and regulatory requirements into solution designs, data requirements, and scoping documents that product, engineering, and sales teams can act on.
• Work with engineering and regulatory experts to validate feasibility, data accuracy, and technical claims before they reach the customer.
Activation, Adoption, and Education
• Define activation and adoption plans for priority customers, covering data setup, integration points, user roles, milestones, and value reviews.
• Educate sellers and customers through webinars, workshops, standards briefings, and associationhosted events that build understanding and demand.
• Diagnose technical and data-related adoption barriers, resolve what falls within scope, and bring in the right expert for the rest.
Commercialization and Market Development
• Identify recurring customer problems that could become repeatable offerings, and help assess which are worth investment.
• Develop technical solution narratives, use cases, reference workflows, and technical-commercial playbooks that scale beyond individual customer engagements.
• Partner with the Business Development Specialist and Commercial Teams to qualify and advance high-potential opportunities.
Industry Association and Standards Partnerships
• Build and maintain working relationships with industry associations, standards development organizations, trade groups, and technical committees relevant to UL Solutions’ digital and compliance offerings.
Data & Innovation
• Represent UL Solutions in technical committees and working groups, contribute to standards and guidance documents, and track changes that affect solution requirements.
• Develop joint activity with associations, including technical webinars, member briefings, white papers, and conference sessions, that builds market understanding of digital compliance.
• Capture technical and regulatory patterns from customer and association engagement and turn them into evidence-based recommendations for Product and leadership.
Required
• Bachelor’s degree in a technical field or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
• Strong technical expertise in a relevant field, such as EMC/wireless, connected products,
conformity assessment, regulatory compliance, or market access.
• Ability to communicate complex technical concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.
• Strong customer-facing presence and the ability to uncover underlying needs and distinguish symptoms from the real problem.
• Ability to influence across functions and organizational levels without relying on direct authority.
• Strong written, presentation, facilitation, and interpersonal communication skills.
• Experience participating in industry associations, standards committees, or technical working groups.
Preferred

The Operations Technician is responsible for the overall safe operation, maintenance, and performance of a landfill gas to Renewable Natural Gas (RNG) processing facility.  This position requires 25%-50% travel per month (First 12 months in the position will require 50% travel per month when hired for a new plant. title: Production Technician
location: United States of America - Louisiana - Shreveport
description:
Job Family Group:
Operations Group
Job Description:
bpx energy, a major oil and gas producer in the United States, leverages its expertise in unconventional gas, including shale, to deliver hydrocarbon production and technical knowledge worldwide. With operations in Texas and Louisiana, our US onshore business has become both a premier oil and gas producer and a leader in reducing methane emissions.
As part of BP, a global industry leader, we foster a high-energy, high-intensity environment built on accountability, collegiality, innovation, and empowerment. At bpx, we support our people to learn and grow in a diverse and challenging environment where safety, operational excellence, continuous improvement, and teamwork are valued.
Discover your place with us and help our business meet the challenges of reimagining and reinventing the future of energy.
Production Technician
ROLE SYNOPSIS:
The Production Technician is a highly motivated, mechanically inclined field operator who supports safe, reliable, and efficient production operations. This hands-on role maintains new and existing wells, equipment, facilities, and infrastructure; performs repairs and preventive maintenance; diagnoses operating issues; and partners across teams to improve equipment performance and operating practices. Success in this role requires a growth mindset, strong problem-solving skills, technical curiosity, and a commitment to safety and continuous improvement.
KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES:
• Work safely in the field with Operations, Maintenance, Engineering, contractor, and other partner teams to support reliable production operations.
• Maintain new and existing wells, equipment, facilities, and related infrastructure.
• Perform repairs and preventive maintenance on production equipment and systems.
• Diagnose operating and equipment issues and conduct basic root cause failure analysis.
• Complete pre-job and post-job reviews and ensure identified actions are communicated and closed out.
• Coordinate and oversee contractor work to support safe, high-quality job execution.
• Collect operating data, validate field conditions, and use available information to support decision-making and problem resolution.
• Investigate customer and third-party issues and coordinate timely resolution with the appropriate teams.
• Support periodic quality assurance reviews and verification of business processes, including safety-related processes.
• Identify defects, variability, and other non-desired outcomes and collaborate across teams to improve operating practices.
• Communicate clearly and effectively with remote staff using phone, video, Microsoft 365, Microsoft Teams, and virtual-assist technology.
• Develop a full-cycle understanding of oil and gas operating systems from the reservoir through the sales line.
• Schedule work activities, remain available to assist others, and build effective cross-functional partnerships.
• Participate actively as a business-unit team member to improve processes and strengthen an interdependent safety culture.
• Use data and available resources to resolve daily field issues and drive continuous improvement.
• Support artificial lift systems, including plunger lift and intermitter wells.
• Close out estimates, complete post-construction checks, update as-built documentation, and review contractor invoices.
• Use databases, mobile applications, and other digital tools to enter and maintain accurate operating data.
ESSENTIAL EXPERIENCE & EDUCATION:
• High school diploma or equivalent.
• At least 3-5 years of relevant oil & gas experience
• Demonstrated mechanical aptitude and interest in hands-on, field-based work.
• Proven problem-solving ability in a similar operating, industrial, or technical environment with measurable business impact.
• Ability to learn and conduct basic failure analysis.
• Experience using data to support decisions and resolve operating issues.
• Working knowledge of artificial lift systems, including plunger lift and intermitter wells.
• Strong aptitude and interest in learning new technology.
• Ability to communicate effectively with field-based and remote team members.
PREFERRED EXPERIENCE:
• Experience in oil and gas, manufacturing, or another industrial business.
• Technical school certificate, associate degree, or related technical education.
• Electrical and mechanical experience in a lean-process environment.
• Instrumentation and electrical, automation, or programming experience.
• Experience managing contractors and supporting safe job execution.
• Experience with databases, data entry, and mobile applications.
PREFERRED ATTRIBUTES:
• Growth mindset with a proven ability to learn and adapt quickly.
• Strong listening and interpersonal skills with an upbeat, inquisitive, and confidence-instilling approach.
• Awareness of desired and non-desired outcomes and a willingness to drive meaningful change.
• Ability to adapt to changing work conditions and manage competing or challenging demands.
• Collaborative approach to continuous improvement and cross-functional problem-solving.
WORKING CONDITIONS:
• Hands-on, field-based work environment.
• Eight-hour shifts, five days per week, with overtime as needed.
• Participation in a seven-day on-call and weekend coverage rotation approximately every fifth or sixth week.
• Periodic use of computers, phones, Microsoft 365, Microsoft Teams, and virtual-assist technology.
• Periodic operation of power equipment.
PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:

location: United States of America - Colorado - Denver
description:

Job Description:
bpx energy, a major oil and gas producer in the United States, leverages its expertise in unconventional gas, including shale, to deliver hydrocarbon production and technical knowledge worldwide. Discover your place with us and help our business meet the challenges of reimagining and reinventing the future of energy.
Role Synopsis
The Eagle Ford Chemical Program position is to protect the long-term integrity and production capacity of the asset through a disciplined, data-driven chemical program. The intent of the role is to work closely with the production and facility engineering teams of the business, chemical SME, and chemical field technician to ensure that every chemical applied in the field is tied to a defined treatment objective — corrosion and scale control, flow assurance, H₂S management, or separation performance — and to a measurable, cost-justified outcome at the well, facility, and route level.
The role is intended to translate operating needs, production data, analytical results, and integrity findings into executable treatment strategies. As well as holding single-point accountability for program performance, vendor delivery, budget, data quality, and continuous improvement across the asset.
Serve as the single point of accountability for the Eagle Ford chemical program, including corrosion inhibitors, scale inhibitors, paraffin treatments, emulsion breakers, methanol, H₂S scavenger, biocides, batch treatments, and other specialty chemicals. Own the program from strategy and planning through field implementation, performance monitoring, optimization, and vendor management.
Key Accountabilities
The role is accountable for cost forecast, budgeting, invoices and purchase orders, chemical-vendor performance, chemical usage optimization, program updates, and coordination of applicable MOCs and work-management activities.
Program Ownership and Optimization
Develop and maintain the Eagle Ford chemical-management strategy, annual plan, budget, performance targets, risks, and improvement roadmap.
Establish treatment philosophies and governance for continuous injection, batch treatments, H₂S scavenging, methanol, emulsion breakers, and specialty applications.
Use production conditions, chemical usage, analytical results, operating feedback, and integrity data to identify under-treatment, over-treatment, poor performance, and cost-reduction opportunities.
Maintain clear roles, escalation paths, decision rights, and handoffs among Program Engineering, Operations, Production Engineering, Facility Engineering, Integrity Management, Finance, Supply Chain, and vendors.
Technical Performance and Integrity
Monitor chemical injection rates, batch-treatment execution, H₂S scavenger efficiency, inhibitor residuals, corrosion coupons, water chemistry, bacteria, solids, emulsions, and oil-analysis results.
Coordinate corrective actions when treatment performance falls outside established targets or analytical data indicates elevated corrosion, scale, bacteria, separation, or flow-assurance risk.
Maintain a closed-loop relationship with Integrity Management so corrosion-monitoring and inspection results inform chemical-treatment decisions, and chemical-program changes trigger reassessment where appropriate.
Support failure investigations and root-cause analyses where chemical performance, corrosion, scale, bacteria, paraffin, emulsion, or H₂S may be contributing factors.
Vendor, Commercial, and Cost Management
Own program-level chemical-vendor relationships and establish expectations for safety, service quality, technical support, chemical delivery, equipment reliability, reporting, responsiveness, and cost.
Lead vendor performance reviews, track actions to closure, and escalate recurring performance issues.
Develop the annual chemical forecast and track actual spending, treatment rates, product costs, and variances.
Validate invoices, purchase orders, delivered volumes, chemical usage, and applicable service charges.
Partner with Supply Chain on sourcing strategies, bid evaluations, contracts, renewals, product trials, and commercial improvements.
Partner with Chemicals Subject Matter Expert on technical oversight, treatment philosophy guidance, chemistry expertise, benchmarking, vendor evaluations, emerging technology assessments, and strategic support for optimization of the Eagle Ford chemical program.
Data, Reporting, and Governance
Maintain accurate chemical inventories, treatment recommendations, injection rates, usage records, analytical results, cost data, vendor actions, and program risks.
Provide routine program updates covering safety, treatment effectiveness, reliability, cost, emerging risks, and required decisions.
Maintain auditable program documentation, technical recommendations, KPI records, vendor reviews, and analytical-data files.
Coordinate MOCs, risk assessments, and site-specific documentation when chemical products, treatment strategies, equipment, or operating conditions change.
Work Environment & Leadership Expectations
Operate effectively in a fast-paced, high-volume environment with shifting priorities and tight execution timelines.
Demonstrate ownership, urgency, adaptability, proactive communication, and disciplined follow-through.
Build productive working relationships across Facilities Engineering, Automation, Operations, Construction, Maintenance, Supply Chain, HSE, vendors, and engineering contractors.
Prioritize competing demands while maintaining design quality, safety, documentation, and stakeholder alignment
Essential Experience and Education
Bachelor’s degree in Chemical Engineering, Petroleum Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Chemistry, or a related technical discipline. Directly relevant experience may be considered in lieu of the specified degree.
Minimum 7 years of progressively responsible experience in upstream oil and gas operations, production chemistry, facilities engineering, integrity management, or chemical-program management.
Minimum 5 years of direct experience supporting U.S. onshore production operations. Candidates without an engineering degree should have at least 10 years of directly relevant oil and gas production-chemistry or chemical-program experience.
Demonstrated ability to lead root-cause investigations and corrective actions involving chemical performance, injection-system reliability, corrosion, scale, bacteria, paraffin, emulsions, or H₂S.
Experience coordinating MOCs, risk assessments, and field implementation activities associated with chemical, equipment, or treatment-strategy changes.
Strong analytical, financial, organizational, written, and verbal communication skills.
Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and experience with operational databases, chemical-management systems, SAP, Power BI, or similar business systems.
Ability to lead cross-functional work across Operations, Engineering, Integrity Management, HSE, Finance, Supply Chain, Maintenance, and chemical vendors.
Ability to travel to field locations, work in operating-facility environments, and comply with applicable field-access, driving, PPE, and HSE requirements.
Desirable Criteria
Demonstrated experience managing or optimizing production-chemical applications such as corrosion inhibitors, scale inhibitors, paraffin treatments, emulsion breakers, H₂S scavengers, methanol, biocides, and batch treatments.
Strong working knowledge of corrosion, scale, bacteria, paraffin, H₂S, emulsions, flow assurance, chemical compatibility, and production-separation performance.
Experience interpreting production data, chemical usage, analytical results, corrosion-monitoring data, water chemistry, bacteria results, oil analysis, and integrity findings to make treatment decisions.
